articles.title: Toward mechanism-informed IVIVC in non-viral gene delivery: From nanoparticle transformation to therapeutic action.
articles.abstract: Gene delivery is now a clinically established modality, but one of its central translational challenges remains: therapeutic performance emerges from a cascade of biological processes rather than from a single step. Lipid nanoparticles, polymeric carriers, and oligonucleotide conjugates undergo biological transformation, distribution and tissue access, cellular uptake, intracellular trafficking, endosomal escape, and ultimately functional payload delivery. The contribution of each process to the therapeutic outcome is context dependent and may shift with formulation, route of administration, target tissue, payload, and disease state. Consequently, transfection efficiency remains a necessary and widely used endpoint, but as a single aggregate readout it cannot by itself indicate which upstream process, biodistribution, uptake, trafficking, or endosomal escape, is rate-limiting for a given formulation, route, or tissue; resolving that bottleneck is the measurable attribute an in vitro-in vivo relationship must be built around. Classical in vitro-in vivo correlation (IVIVC) concepts were developed for simpler relationships, but their underlying principle remains relevant: identifying a measurable product attribute or process that governs in vivo performance. As pharmaceutical systems have become more complex, biopredictive methodologies have logically progressed toward process-resolved assays, systems-level understanding, and mechanistic modeling. Applying this principle to non-viral gene delivery does not imply that a validated IVIVC, or a regulatory biowaiver built on one, yet exists for these systems; rather, it asks whether the same underlying logic, identifying which step in a multi-step cascade is rate limiting and can be represented by a measurable in vitro assay, can be meaningfully extended from simpler dosage forms to a biologically complex delivery process. This review proposes a pathway toward IVIVC for non-viral gene delivery as a delivery cascade comprising three interconnected layers: (i) the Nanoparticle Biodistribution Layer, spanning circulation, biological transformation, and tissue access; (ii) the Cellular Delivery Dynamics Layer, encompassing cellular uptake, intracellular trafficking, and endosomal escape; and (iii) the Functional Therapeutic Action Layer, linking productive delivery to pharmacodynamic response. Each layer is matched with assays that isolate individual processes and expose where formulation performance becomes limiting. These layers have traditionally been studied by largely separate scientific communities, making their integration essential for understanding how performance gains or losses propagate through the delivery cascade. Rather than proposing a holistic IVIVC that does not yet exist for non-viral gene delivery, this framework provides a mechanistic roadmap for building it, moving formulation development from empirical screening toward stepwise biopredictive evidence and, ultimately, IVIVC for complex gene delivery systems.

articles.title: The environmental fates, exposure routes, and human health implications of liquid crystal monomers: an emerging global contaminant.
articles.abstract: Liquid crystal monomers (LCMs), as the core functional molecules in liquid crystal displays, have become pervasive environmental contaminants. Of these, fluorinated and cyano-substituted LCMs garnered particular attention due to their pronounced persistence, bioaccumulation, and toxicity features. However, their exposure routes, ecological and human hazards, potential biological mechanisms, and the remediation technologies remain inadequately defined. This review addresses these gaps by tracing the environmental behaviors and fates of LCMs, thereby establishing a foundation for prioritizing these compounds and designing safer molecules. The primary routes for LCMs to enter the human body include inhalation, ingestion, and dermal contact. It is noteworthy that the pervasive exposure to LCMs contributes to the extensive detection of LCMs in serum, urine, and even breast milk. Furthermore, infants, children, and e-waste workers were identified as priority populations of concern. In particular, LCMs induce a spectrum of deleterious effects in microorganisms, aquatic organisms, terrestrial organisms, and mammals. Despite the promise of contemporary remediation technologies, their large-scale implementation remains a formidable challenge. By integrating molecular characteristics, exposure pathways, and population-level risk assessment, this review provides a foundation for dissecting its exposure route, mitigated its toxicological effects, and the development of lower-risk liquid crystal materials.

articles.title: Targeting the pyroptosis network: Research progress of natural products in intervention for acute lung injury.
articles.abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) is a serious clinical condition with high morbidity and mortality rates. Current ALI treatments have limitations. Natural products from traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) exhibit multi-component, multi-target and multi-pathway regulatory properties with good safety, making them promising candidates for ALI treatment. This review systematically summarizes the activation pathways of pyroptosis, its molecular regulatory network in ALI and the mechanisms by which natural products regulate pyroptosis to inhibit ALI progression. A 'natural products-pyroptosis-ALI' axis conceptual framework is proposed to provide theoretical support for clinical translation. Systematic literature searches were conducted on CNKI, Web of Science and PubMed up to March 2026, using keywords related to natural products, ALI and pyroptosis. This review covers TCM herbs, natural small-molecule compounds and TCM formulas that modulate pyroptosis to alleviate ALI, with all animal experiments adhering to ethical and international standards. Various natural products and TCM formulae effectively target pyroptosis, inhibiting NLRP3 inflammasome assembly, Caspase-1 activation and Gasdermin D pore formation, thereby reducing IL-1β/IL-18 release, alleviating inflammatory cascades, protecting alveolar-capillary barrier integrity and mitigating oxidative stress. Activated pyroptosis further disturbs mitophagy, triggers endoplasmic reticulum stress, engages the gut-lung axis, modulates epigenetic reprogramming and promotes epithelial-mesenchymal transition to amplify ALI. This review fills gaps in the systematic characterization of pyroptosis-ALI relationships and natural product-based therapies, aiming to expand ALI treatment options and advance ALI therapeutic development.

articles.title: Betel quid-induced oral carcinogenesis: emerging insights into genotoxicity, epigenetic aberration, and immune dysregulation.
articles.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is a global health burden, particularly in South and Southeast Asia, where betel quid (BQ) chewing remains highly prevalent. As epidemiological evidence consistently identifies BQ as an independent risk factor for OSCC, recent high-throughput sequencing analyses and experimental mutagenesis studies have substantially advanced our understanding of the biological mechanisms underlying BQ-related oral tumorigenesis. This review provides an updated overview of the molecular and cellular alterations associated with chronic BQ exposure during OSCC development, with particular emphasis on genotoxicity, epigenetic and noncoding RNA-mediated remodeling, and immune dysregulation. BQ and its related constituents induce diverse forms of genomic instability in oral tissues, including chromosomal abnormalities, impaired DNA repair, characteristic mutational spectra/signatures, copy-number alterations, and loss of heterozygosity. Concurrently, chronic BQ exposure promotes widespread epigenetic dysregulation through altered DNA methylation, histone modification, and noncoding RNA-mediated pathways, resulting in silencing of tumor suppressor genes and activation of oncogenic signaling. Emerging evidence also suggests that BQ exposure may reshape the immune microenvironment of OSCC into a permissive niche for tumor progression and therapeutic resistance, highlighted by increased infiltration of tumor-associated macrophages, altered immunoregulatory dendritic cell programs, and activation of immune checkpoint pathways such as PD-L1/PD-1 and CD155/TIGIT. Collectively, these findings suggest that BQ-related OSCC may represent an etiologically defined subgroup of oral cancer with partially distinct genomic, epigenetic, and immunologic features, although further validation across anatomical sites, exposure patterns, and population backgrounds is required. A better understanding of these alterations may facilitate the development of novel prognostic biomarkers and precision therapeutic strategies for BQ-related oral cancer.

articles.title: Model-informed characterisation of the target therapeutic window for dexamethasone by quantitatively balancing foetal lung maturation and neurotoxicity in pregnant rats.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Dexamethasone, a first-line treatment for neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (NRDS), promotes foetal lung maturation whilst simultaneously inducing neurotoxicity in offspring. We aimed to define the therapeutic window of dexamethasone for the treatment of NRDS. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Pregnant rats were given dexamethasone at 0.1 or 0.4 mg·kg-1 to simulate clinically equivalent prenatal dexamethasone exposure. Half of the rats were anaesthetised, and surfactant proteins A and B in foetal lungs quantified. A pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamics (PK/PD) model was developed to determine the minimum effective concentration. The remaining rats, delivered naturally, and their offspring underwent open-field testing. Messenger RNA sequencing of the foetal hippocampus was performed, and concentration-toxicity assays were conducted using H19-7/IGF-IR cells. Data were integrated with a maternal-foetal physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model to determine the maximum tolerated concentration. A clinical PBPK for dexamethasone in pregnant women was used to simulate a potentially optimal dosing regimen. KEY RESULTS: The PK/PD model adequately characterised dexamethasone-induced foetal lung maturation and indicated a minimal effective concentration of 1.63 ng·ml-1. The offspring of PDE rats exhibited significant behavioural changes. mRNA sequencing analysis suggested that neurotoxicity was mediated via the Wnt pathway and renin-angiotensin system, with BDNF and CMA1 identified as potential biomarkers of neurotoxicity. Cell-based assays suggested a neurotoxic threshold concentration of 17 ng·ml-1. For a therapeutic window of 1.63-17 ng·ml-1, PBPK model simulations indicated that a reduced dose regimen of 2.5 or 3 mg every 8 h for six doses may represent an optimised therapeutic strategy. CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: This model-informed precision dosing strategy provides a rational approach to optimising clinical dexamethasone dosing regimens.

articles.title: The Evidence Journey in Patient-Centered Medicine Development: Reflections on Recent Publications in Clinical Pharmacology & Therapeutics.
articles.abstract: This Commentary highlights the evidence journey in patient-centered medicine development: inter-disciplinary innovations in quantitative methods for Probability of Success enabling rigorous decision-making; decentralized clinical trials and implementation research enabling patient-focused medicine development and deployment; and real-world evidence, enabled by high-quality data and advanced analytics, transforming decision-making by regulators and health technology assessors. Multidisciplinary, cross-sector collaboration and patient input are essential throughout the medicine lifecycle.

articles.title: December 2026 issue first authors.
L-Alanine Inhibits the AKI-to-CKD Transition by Restoring MCT2-Mediated Metabolic Reprogramming in Tubular Epithelial Cells.
articles.abstract: Dysregulated amino acid metabolism is a prominent feature after acute kidney injury (AKI), but its contribution to chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression remains unclear. The therapeutic potential of targeting these metabolic alterations also remains poorly understood. Quantification of 20 circulating L-amino acids revealed that L-alanine (Ala) showed the most pronounced reduction in patients with cardiac surgery-associated AKI and renal ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) mice. Notably, supplementation of exogenous Ala attenuated the AKI-to-CKD transition in IRI mice. Mechanistically, Ala restored monocarboxylate transporter 2 (MCT2) expression by preventing heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein M (hnRNPM)-mediated destabilization of D-box binding protein (DBP) mRNA. Subsequently, DBP was identified as a transcriptional regulator of MCT2 and enhanced its transcription by directly binding to its promoter region. Furthermore, renal tubular epithelial cell (RTEC)-specific deletion of MCT2 blunted Ala-mediated restoration of mitochondrial oxidative metabolism and renal protection. These findings reveal a mechanism by which Ala promotes tubular metabolic recovery and provide preclinical evidence supporting further evaluation of Ala supplementation to limit AKI-to-CKD progression after cardiac surgery.

articles.title: Shenlingcao oral liquid suppresses colorectal cancer by reprogramming the immune microenvironment and inhibiting pro-tumorigenic inflammation.
articles.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, yet most patients are refractory to immunotherapy. Shenlingcao oral liquid (SOL), a traditional Chinese medicine formula with established chemosensitizing activity in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), remains to be systematically evaluated in CRC. Building on our prior demonstration of SOL efficacy in orthotopic and metastatic NSCLC models, we report concordant tissue pharmacokinetic profiles of its major bioactive constituents across lung, intestine and spleen, providing a pharmacological rationale for evaluating its activity in CRC. Using two etiologically distinct CRC models-inflammation-driven and APC-mutant mouse models, integrated multi-omics profiling and functional validation, we demonstrate that SOL suppresses colorectal tumorigenesis and prolongs survival associated with two complementary mechanisms. Specifically, SOL remodels the gut microbiota and bile acid metabolism, activates of FXR-dependent protective programs, restores intestinal barrier integrity, and selectively suppresses aberrant Wnt signaling in inflammation-associated colorectal carcinogenesis, an effect further validated in DSS-induced colitis. Furthermore, SOL consistently promotes intratumoral CD8+ T-cell infiltration and upregulates the immunoglobulin complex (IG) gene expression across both models. Elevated IG gene signature status was associated with favorable prognosis and enhanced immune infiltration in patients with APC-mutant CRC. Accordingly, SOL potentiated PD-1 blockade in both microsatellite-stable and microsatellite instability-high CRC models, as well as in an orthotopic NSCLC model, supporting a conserved immunomodulatory mechanism. Together, our findings demonstrate that SOL suppresses colorectal tumorigenesis through coordinated inhibiting of pro-tumorigenic inflammation and reprogramming of the tumor immune microenvironment, providing a mechanistic rationale for developing SOL as a multitarget therapeutic strategy for CRC prevention and immunotherapy sensitization.

articles.title: Periplogenin rewires cholesterol-dependent signaling and antitumor immunity by targeting PCSK9 in cholangiocarcinoma.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is an aggressive malignancy with limited therapeutic options, underscoring the need to identify novel therapeutic agents and actionable molecular targets. PURPOSE: This study aimed to identify natural compounds with antitumor activity against CCA and to elucidate their molecular mechanisms and therapeutic potential. STUDY DESIGN: A phenotype-based natural-product screening strategy was combined with mechanistic, genetic, multi-omics, and in vivo validation to identify and characterize periplogenin (PPG) as a candidate therapeutic agent for CCA. METHODS: The antitumor effects of PPG were evaluated using CCA cells, organoids, xenograft models, orthotopic tumor models, and immunocompetent CCA models. Integrative proteomic analyses were performed to identify PPG-regulated pathways. Molecular docking, Cellular Thermal Shift Assay (CETSA) and Drug Affinity Responsive Target Stability (DARTS) assays were used to determine the direct molecular target of PPG, followed by PCSK9 knockout and methyl-β-cyclodextrin (MβCD) to assess target dependency and downstream mechanisms. Single-cell RNA sequencing was employed to characterize PPG-induced remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment, and the therapeutic efficacy of PPG combined with anti-PD-L1 treatment was further evaluated in vivo. RESULTS: PPG significantly suppressed CCA organoid outgrowth and metastatic potential, restrained tumorigenesis, and prolonged survival in orthotopic and xenograft CCA models. Integrative proteomics identified cholesterol metabolism and PI3K-AKT signaling as major pathways altered by PPG. PPG directly bound proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) and reduced PCSK9 abundance by promoting lysosomal degradation. Functionally, PPG increased cellular cholesterol and remodeled cholesterol-dependent membrane microdomains (lipid rafts), thereby attenuating PI3K-AKT activation. Cholesterol depletion with methyl-β-cyclodextrin blunted these effects. Genetic ablation of PCSK9 largely occluded PPG-induced cholesterol-lipid raft remodeling and diminished its antitumor efficacy, supporting PCSK9 dependence. Single-cell RNA sequencing further revealed that PPG increased cytotoxic CD8+ T-cell infiltration while reducing exhausted CD8+ T cells. Moreover, PPG potentiated anti-PD-L1 therapy and achieved superior tumor control in immunocompetent CCA models. CONCLUSION: PPG exerts potent antitumor activity in CCA by directly targeting PCSK9 and inducing PCSK9-dependent cholesterol-membrane remodeling, which suppresses oncogenic PI3K-AKT signaling and enhances antitumor immunity. These findings identify PCSK9 as a druggable target of PPG and support PPG as a potential therapeutic strategy for CCA, particularly in combination with immune checkpoint blockade.

articles.title: Huachansu combined with chemotherapy for advanced gastrointestinal malignancies: a systematic review and meta-analysis with formulation-stratified analyses.
articles.abstract: AIM: To evaluate the clinical effects of Huachansu combined plus chemotherapy compared with chemotherapy alone in advanced gastrointestinal malignancies and to explore potential variation in treatment-effect estimates across Huachansu formulations. METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang database, Chinese Science and Technology Journal Database (VIP), and SinoMed (CBM) were searched from inception to 27 May 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing Huachansu plus chemotherapy with chemotherapy alone were included. Forty-three RCTs involving 3,255 participants and three Huachansu formulations (injection, capsule, and tablet) were eligible. Primary outcomes were disease control rate (DCR) and objective response rate (ORR). Secondary outcomes included overall survival (OS), 3-year survival rate, quality of life, tumor markers, immune indices, angiogenic factors, and reported treatment-related adverse events. RESULTS: Compared to chemotherapy alone, Huachansu combined with chemotherapy was associated with higher DCR (RR = 1.20, 95% CI: 1.16-1.24) and ORR (RR = 1.42, 95% CI: 1.33-1.51). Formulation-stratified analyses identified a significant subgroup difference for DCR (χ2 = 10.25, P = 0.006), but not for ORR (χ2 = 4.75, P = 0.09). Survival data suggested a potential association with longer overall survival (MD = 2.02 months, 95% CI: 1.42 to 2.63; 2 RCTs) and a higher 3-year survival rate (RR = 1.96, 95% CI: 1.20 to 3.20; 3 RCTs). Tumor-biomarker analyses suggested associations with lower CEA (SMD = -1.59, 95% CI: -2.05 to -1.12; I2 = 91%), CA19-9 (SMD = -1.35, 95% CI: -1.78 to -0.92; I2 = 89%), and CA125 (SMD = -1.16, 95% CI: -1.47 to -0.84; I2 = 64%). Favorable changes were also reported in quality-of-life and selected immune- and angiogenesis-related outcomes. Lower reported incidences of gastrointestinal reactions, oral mucositis, peripheral neuropathy, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, and hepatic/renal injury were observed. CONCLUSION: Huachansu plus chemotherapy may provide additional clinical benefits in advanced gastrointestinal malignancies, with higher short-term tumor response rates, greater improvements in quality of life, and lower adverse events. Changes in tumor, immune, and angiogenesis-related biomarkers offer exploratory biological insights. Formulation-stratified findings remain inconclusive because of indirect comparisons, and further high-quality, adequately powered RCTs are warranted. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO identifier CRD420261406854.

articles.title: Protective effects and mechanisms of polyphenols in animal models of testicular dysfunction: a preclinical systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Testicular dysfunction is a significant contributor to male infertility, characterized by impaired spermatogenesis, reduced testosterone production, and structural damage to testicular tissue. Polyphenols, a class of naturally occurring plant metabolites abundant in fruits, vegetables, and plant-derived beverages, show considerable promise in ameliorating testicular dysfunction in animal models. Their protective effects are primarily mediated through antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic mechanisms, along with the modulation of steroidogenic pathways. This study examines the effects of polyphenols on testicular dysfunction in experimental animal models. METHODS: A systematic search of six electronic databases (PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, the Web of Science Core Collection, China National Knowledge Infrastructure and Wanfang Data) was performed using keywords related to polyphenols and testicular dysfunction. The analysis incorporated preclinical animal studies evaluating polyphenol interventions for testicular injury. The methodological quality of the included studies was assessed using the CAMARADES checklist. This review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251171737). RESULTS: A total of 46 studies involving 1,252 animals were included. The meta-analysis demonstrated that polyphenols: 1) Improved sperm parameters, significantly increasing sperm count [SMD = 3.36, 95% CI (1.62, 5.09), P < 0.0001] and progressive sperm motility [SMD = 6.95, 95% CI (4.54, 8.96), P < 0.0001], while reducing sperm abnormality rate [SMD = -5.70, 95% CI (-8.42, -2.97), P < 0.0001]; 2) Enhanced testicular structure, significantly increasing seminiferous tubule diameter [SMD = 3.91, 95% CI (1.46, 6.36), P < 0.01], germinal epithelium height [SMD = 4.70, 95% CI (2.34, 7.06), P < 0.0001], and epididymal weight [SMD = 1.98, 95% CI (0.08, 3.89), P < 0.05]; 3) Elevated serum testosterone concentration [SMD = 2.72, 95% CI (1.93, 3.50), P < 0.0001]; 4) Attenuated oxidative stress, decreasing ROS [SMD = -4.91, 95% CI (-7.10, -2.72), P < 0.0001] and MDA levels [SMD = -4.63, 95% CI (-6.18, -3.09), P < 0.0001], while increasing SOD [SMD = 4.41, 95% CI (2.46, 6.35), P < 0.0001] and GSH [SMD = 4.72, 95% CI (3.02, 6.43), P < 0.0001] activities; 5) Suppressed inflammatory responses, reducing TNF-α [SMD = -4.06, 95% CI (-5.70, -2.42), P < 0.0001], IL-6 [SMD = -8.46, 95% CI (-13.44, -3.48), P < 0.01], and COX-2 [SMD = -8.50, 95% CI (-15.85, -1.16), P < 0.05] levels; 6) Inhibited apoptosis, decreasing Caspase-3 [SMD = -8.52, 95% CI (-10.72, -6.32), P < 0.0001] and Caspase-9 [SMD = -4.29, 95% CI (-7.58, -1.00), P < 0.05] expression; 7) Enhanced steroidogenesis, increasing 3β-HSD activity [SMD = 4.24, 95% CI (1.96, 6.53), P < 0.001]. CONCLUSION: Polyphenols significantly ameliorate testicular dysfunction in animal models by activating the Nrf2/ARE antioxidant pathway, inhibiting NF-κB-mediated inflammatory signaling, suppressing mitochondrial apoptotic cascades, and preserving steroidogenic enzyme function. Future research should focus on translating these promising preclinical findings into clinically effective interventions for male reproductive disorders. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251171737, identifier CRD420251171737.

articles.title: Comparative efficacy and safety of nonhormonal prescription drugs for vasomotor symptoms in women with breast cancer: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Vasomotor symptoms (VMS) are common during and after breast cancer treatment, particularly among women receiving endocrine therapy. We compared the efficacy, acceptability, and safety of nonhormonal prescription pharmacological interventions for VMS in women with breast cancer or breast cancer survivors. METHODS: We searched major databases and trial registries through July 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing nonhormonal prescription drugs versus placebo or another eligible nonhormonal prescription drug in adult women with breast cancer-related VMS. The primary outcome was continuous VMS efficacy. Secondary outcomes included responder outcomes, all-cause discontinuation, discontinuation due to adverse events, any adverse events, and serious adverse events. We performed frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis, with Bayesian network meta-analysis as sensitivity analysis. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, and certainty of evidence using a GRADE/NMA-GRADE approach. RESULTS: Eighteen publications, corresponding to 19 study/substudy records and 2,224 randomized or allocated participants, were included. Five interventions were significantly more effective than placebo: escitalopram (SMD -1.08, 95% CI -1.80 to -0.37), desvenlafaxine 50 mg (SMD -0.87, 95% CI -1.60 to -0.15), desvenlafaxine 100 mg (SMD -0.80, 95% CI -1.44 to -0.15), elinzanetant (SMD -0.51, 95% CI -0.95 to -0.07), and venlafaxine 75 mg (SMD -0.42, 95% CI -0.76 to -0.07). Heterogeneity was moderate (I2 = 44.9%), with no significant global or local inconsistency. Frequentist P-scores ranked the five significant drugs top, confirmed by Bayesian sensitivity. Elinzanetant had high-certainty evidence, whereas venlafaxine 75 mg and gabapentin 900 mg had moderate-certainty evidence. Escitalopram and desvenlafaxine had large effects, but the supporting evidence was sparse. Discontinuation outcomes showed no statistically significant differences versus placebo, but sparse safety networks precluded a reliable comparative safety hierarchy; these null findings should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalent tolerability. CONCLUSION: Nonhormonal prescription drugs are not interchangeable for breast cancer-related VMS. Elinzanetant provides the strongest high-certainty evidence among newer targeted options, and venlafaxine 75 mg is the best-supported conventional option. Escitalopram and desvenlafaxine remain promising but require further trials. Gabapentin 900 mg may be considered in selected patients, whereas sertraline, bupropion, gabapentin 300 mg, and clonidine are lower-priority options. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261460108, identifier CRD420261460108.

articles.title: Insulin Efsitora Alfa: First Approval.
articles.abstract: Insulin efsitora alfa (Onswik™) is a once-weekly ultra-long-acting recombinant basal insulin being developed by Eli Lilly and Company for the treatment of diabetes mellitus. Administered once weekly as a subcutaneous injection, insulin efsitora alfa is designed to provide a simplified treatment regimen relative to standard daily basal insulins. On 20 August 2026, insulin efsitora alfa received its first approval in the EU for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) in adults. On 24 September 2026, insulin efsitora alfa was approved in the USA as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with T2DM. Insulin efsitora alfa is approved in the EU, Iceland, Norway, Liechtenstein and the USA and is under regulatory review in the UK and Japan for T2DM. This article summarizes the milestones in the development of insulin efsitora alfa leading to this first approval for T2DM.

articles.title: Daraxonrasib: First Approval.
articles.abstract: Daraxonrasib (RASONQUE™) is an oral, multiselective, noncovalent RAS(ON) inhibitor being developed by Revolution Medicines for the treatment of solid tumours, including pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), non-small-cell lung cancer and colorectal cancer. Daraxonrasib received its first approval in the USA on 26 August 2026 for the treatment of adults with metastatic PDAC who have received at least one prior systemic therapy or who are not candidates for multiagent systemic therapy. This article summarizes the milestones in the development of daraxonrasib leading to its first approval for metastatic PDAC.

articles.title: Oveporexton: First Approval.
articles.abstract: Oveporexton (ORZEYFULTM) is an oral selective orexin receptor 2 agonist developed by Takeda Pharmaceuticals Inc. for the treatment of narcolepsy type 1 (NT1). Oveporexton received its first approval in China on 22 July 2026 for the treatment of adolescents aged ≥ 16 years and adults with NT1. Subsequently, oveporexton was approved on 5 August 2026 in the USA and on 24 August 2026 in Japan for adults with NT1. Targeting the underlying orexin deficiency in NT1, oveporexton is the first and only agent approved for the treatment of NT1 addressing the full range of symptoms which define the condition. Additional global filings and phase III clinical trials are ongoing. This article summarizes the milestones in the development of oveporexton leading to this first approval for NT1.

articles.title: Yupingfeng San ameliorates lipopolysaccharide-induced acute intestinal inflammation via modulation of the MAPK/apoptosis signaling pathway.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Yupingfeng San (YPFS) is a traditional Chinese medicine formulation traditionally used to tonify Wei Qi and consolidate the exterior. Its anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory activities provide a pharmacological basis for investigation in inflammation. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study investigated the protective effects and underlying mechanisms of YPFS against lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced acute intestinal inflammation using network pharmacology, transcriptomics, molecular docking, and in vivo experiments. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Putative active compounds, targets, and pathways were identified by network pharmacology and enrichment analysis. An LPS-induced acute intestinal inflammation mouse model was established, and clinical, histopathological, inflammatory, transcriptomic, and molecular outcomes were evaluated. MAPK- and apoptosis-associated changes were examined by RT-qPCR and Western blotting. RESULTS: Network analysis identified quercetin, decursin, astragaloside IV, ledebouriellol A, and formononetin as key compounds, with Tnf, Mapk1, Mapk3, Il1b, and Casp3 as core targets. YPFS pretreatment improved clinical manifestations, reduced DAI and organ indices, alleviated colonic injury, and improved goblet-cell loss. YPFS reduced IL-1β and TNF-α, increased IL-4 and IL-10, and improved ZO-1 and Occludin mRNA expression. Transcriptomic and qRT-PCR analyses indicated that YPFS modulated MAPK- and apoptosis-associated gene expression. Western blotting further showed reduced LPS-associated ERK and JNK phosphorylation and attenuation of apoptosis-associated protein changes, including BAX, BCL-2, and Cleaved-caspase-3. CONCLUSIONS: YPFS attenuated LPS-associated acute intestinal inflammatory injury and inhibited aberrant MAPK signaling, accompanied by attenuation of apoptosis-associated molecular changes and improvement of barrier-associated morphological and transcriptional alterations. These findings support the potential involvement of the MAPK/apoptosis axis in the protective effects of YPFS.

articles.title: Bidirectional interplay of the gut microbiota and herbal medicine in Alzheimer's disease: mechanisms and therapeutic prospects.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder in which alterations in the gut microbiota and microbiota-gut-brain axis (MGBA) may contribute to disease-related pathological processes. Herbal medicines have long been used for memory impairment and age-related cognitive disorders and contain bioactive constituents with diverse molecular targets. Increasing evidence suggests that herbal interventions can modulate the gut microbiota, while gut microorganisms can biotransform selected herbal constituents and influence their absorption and biological activity. These reciprocal interactions provide a mechanistic basis for investigating herbal medicine in AD. AIM OF THE REVIEW: This review summarizes the bidirectional interactions between herbal medicine and the gut microbiota in AD, focusing on microbial composition and metabolites, intestinal barrier function, herbal biotransformation and bioavailability, signaling pathways, and multi-omics approaches. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A structured narrative literature review was conducted using PubMed, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect for studies published from January 2010 to June 2026. Google Scholar searches and reference-list screening supplemented the database searches. Human, animal, and in vitro studies concerning AD, gut microbiota, herbal interventions, microbial metabolites, biotransformation, and bioavailability were included according to predefined eligibility criteria. RESULTS: Herbal formulas, extracts, and compounds have been reported to alter gut microbial composition and metabolite profiles, improve intestinal barrier integrity, and influence inflammatory, oxidative, amyloid-β (Aβ)-related, and synaptic pathways relevant to AD. Conversely, the gut microbiota can biotransform selected herbal constituents, thereby altering their absorption and pharmacological properties. Integrated microbiome-metabolome studies also link microbial taxa, metabolites, and host signaling pathways, but most findings remain preclinical or correlational. CONCLUSIONS: The bidirectional interaction between herbal medicine and the gut microbiota may be relevant to AD treatment. However, current evidence is largely preclinical and clinical validation remains limited. Future studies should clarify microbiota-dependent biotransformation and pharmacokinetics, standardize herbal formulas and dosing, establish causal microbe-metabolite-host relationships, assess long-term safety and herb-drug interactions, and conduct rigorous clinical trials before translation into AD management.

articles.title: Biomarkers and molecular determinants of T-cell engager response, resistance and toxicity.
articles.abstract: T-cell engagers redirect endogenous T cells against malignant cells and have produced clinically meaningful responses across haematological malignancies and selected solid tumours. Responses vary, while cytokine release syndrome, neurotoxicity, infection and on-target, off-tumour injury constrain treatment. Target positivity alone is therefore insufficient for selecting patients, molecules or dosing strategies. This Review synthesises evidence across five interacting domains: host immune reserve and T-cell fitness; engager molecular design and pharmacology; tumour antigen ecology and genomic vulnerability; the tumour immune ecosystem; and toxicity risk. Productive engagement requires functionally competent T cells, adequate active exposure at the tumour site, accessible and persistent antigen, tissue trafficking and calibrated T-cell activation. Candidate host markers include circulating lymphocyte and T-cell subsets, differentiation and exhaustion states, systemic inflammation, prior immunotherapy and microbiome-metabolic features. Molecular format, pharmacokinetics, activation threshold and synapse geometry influence the balance between cytotoxicity and systemic inflammation. Antigen density, coverage, accessibility, heterogeneity and treatment-induced loss shape sensitivity and resistance, whereas suppressive immune cells, stroma and metabolic constraints restrict tissue activity. Circulating tumour DNA, measurable residual disease and soluble antigen can support longitudinal response assessment. Baseline inflammation, cytokine kinetics and normal immune-lineage depletion may inform safety monitoring, but risk factors, pharmacodynamic changes, early-warning signals and manifestations of established toxicity serve different purposes. Most reported markers remain prognostic, pharmacodynamic or useful for resistance classification rather than validated predictors of treatment benefit. Clinical translation requires standardised assays, context-specific thresholds, external validation and prospective trials showing that biomarker-guided decisions improve patient outcomes.

articles.title: Drp1 structure, assembly, and cardiovascular pharmacology: lessons and limits of Mdivi-1.
articles.abstract: Dynamin-related protein 1 (Drp1) is a mechanoenzyme that moves between autoinhibited, receptor-bound, oligomeric and membrane-constricting states. This structural plasticity creates several pharmacological opportunities, but it also limits the interpretation of mitochondrial division inhibitor 1 (Mdivi-1), the most widely used fission-modulating compound in cardiovascular research. We integrate experimental Drp1 structures with biochemical pharmacology, cell-specific cardiovascular biology and translational evidence. A ligand-bound Drp1 structure (Protein Data Bank entry 8SKN) provided a positive-control pocket for an exploratory docking analysis. Redocking of the co-crystal ligand failed in a dry preparation (0/20 seeds) but succeeded after four crystallographic waters were retained (20/20; median top-three root-mean-square deviation, 0.83 Å). Three prespecified Mdivi-1 tautomers then produced reproducible poses in this pocket, although their median Vina scores were 2.11-2.39 kcal/mol less favorable than that of the co-crystal ligand. These calculations support geometric compatibility under one validated preparation; they do not establish direct binding, inhibition or selectivity. Mdivi-1 also affects complex I, respiratory supercomplexes, redox state, autophagic flux, calcium handling and cardiovascular ion channels. Drp1 itself supports both injurious fragmentation and adaptive quality control, with outcomes that vary by cell type and disease phase. Structure, exposure and cellular context together inform the cardiovascular response. Mdivi-1 remains a useful mechanistic probe whose contribution to Drp1-dependent function is clarified through target engagement and independent causal evidence.

articles.title: The role of polo-like kinase 1 (PLK1) in non-small cell lung cancer: molecular mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
articles.abstract: Polo-like kinase 1 (PLK1) is a highly conserved serine/threonine kinase that orchestrates key processes in mitotic progression, DNA damage repair, apoptosis, and immune signaling. Its frequent overexpression in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) correlates with tumor aggressiveness, poor prognosis, and resistance to therapy, highlighting its significance as both a biomarker and therapeutic target. This review systematically evaluates the molecular mechanisms by which PLK1 drives NSCLC pathogenesis, including its regulation by transcription factors, tumor suppressors, oncogenes, non-coding RNAs, and signaling pathways. We highlight PLK1's role in promoting cell cycle progression, chromosomal instability, metastasis, immune escape, and therapeutic resistance to chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and targeted agents. Furthermore, we summarize preclinical and clinical advances in PLK1-directed therapies, encompassing small-molecule inhibitors, RNA interference, gene editing, PROTACs, and nanomedicine-based strategies, with an emphasis on their potential to enhance sensitivity to existing treatments. Collectively, current evidence establishes PLK1 as a central hub in NSCLC biology and a promising candidate for precision oncology. Future investigations should prioritize biomarker-driven clinical trials, combinatorial strategies, and next-generation inhibitors for overcoming resistance and improving patient outcomes.

articles.title: Animal-derived anticoagulant peptides and small proteins from snake venom and tick saliva: Mechanisms, structural biochemistry, and translational barriers.
articles.abstract: Animal-derived anticoagulant peptides and small proteins from snake venom and tick saliva are valuable but underexploited molecular prototypes for antithrombotic drug discovery. Snake venom evolved under predation pressure, whereas tick saliva has been refined through long-term blood feeding. Despite their distinct origins, both systems have generated compact cysteine-rich scaffolds that interfere potently with host hemostasis. This review compares representative anticoagulant peptides and small proteins from snake venoms and tick saliva, focusing on structural features, mechanisms, and translational potential. A curated dataset of 56 tick-derived and 61 snake-derived sequences was analyzed to identify shared structural constraints and divergent functional features. Mechanistically, these molecules target multiple coagulation nodes including the TF/FVIIa complex, contact pathway, FXa and thrombin activity, platelet aggregation, and fibrin formation. Beyond classical active-site blockade, we discuss allosteric inhibition via exosite occupancy exemplified by ixolaris and the active-site-inhibited derivative FFR-notecarin D, while noting that native notecarin D is a prothrombin activator and is not itself an anticoagulant. In silico docking of representative peptides, including TAP, ultravariegin, BF9-N17K-L19D, and ACH-11, was performed to generate structural hypotheses. Major translational barriers such as immunogenicity, rapid renal clearance, low oral bioavailability, and source scarcity are reinterpreted from a structural perspective. We conclude by outlining possible future directions, including AI-guided scaffold cyclization, exosite-selective mutagenesis, and responsive nanocarrier-peptide conjugates, which may contribute to the development of potentially safer FXI and FXII targeted antithrombotics if validated experimentally. Integrating structural biology, computational prediction, and mechanism-guided engineering will be essential to convert these natural prototypes into clinically relevant therapeutics.

articles.title: From Pt-DNA lesions to cGAS-STING activation: Molecular pharmacology of cold-to-hot tumor reprogramming.
articles.abstract: Platinum drugs can generate immune signals through DNA damage, organelle stress, and effects on immune cells. This review presents a lesion-sensing-immunity framework linking platinum exposure and lesion processing to DNA accessibility, cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS) catalysis, stimulator of interferon genes (STING) activation, and antitumor immunity. Clinically used platinum(II) agents are distinguished from engineered platinum(IV) prodrugs, including constructs delivering direct STING agonists. Selected preclinical models establish contributions from STING, mitochondrial DNA, and tumor-to-myeloid communication, supporting combinations guided by mechanistic evidence and pharmacology. Emerging intervention opportunities include releasing cGAS from nucleosome sequestration, preserving extracellular cyclic GMP-AMP (cGAMP), modulating STING trafficking, engaging complementary RNA sensing, and targeting antigen-presenting cells. Platinum combinations with ectonucleotide pyrophosphatase/phosphodiesterase 1 (ENPP1) inhibitors exemplify signal preservation. Negative and conflicting findings emphasize the importance of substrate state, assay timing, cell viability, and responding-cell identity. Evidence grading separates negative results, tumor-promoting mechanisms, and incomplete causal attribution, without equating DNA damage with immune activation. Randomized chemoimmunotherapy trials establish regimen-level efficacy but do not resolve component-specific immune mechanisms. We propose a framework integrating pharmacokinetics, biotransformation, and pharmacodynamics with chemically defined exposure, DNA lesions, pathway engagement, immune function, and host tolerance. This framework supports testable strategies for translating platinum-associated injury into productive antitumor immunity.

articles.title: Established conditions for analytical procedures: Scientific principles, current state, and practical considerations.
articles.abstract: Established Conditions (ECs) for analytical procedures, introduced in ICH Q12 and further elaborated in ICH Q14, provides a science- and risk-based framework for managing post-approval changes of analytical procedures in a more predictable and efficient manner. Despite the framework's availability since 2019, global adoption in regulatory submissions has remained low across most major regions and submission types, with a particularly notable absence in generic drug applications. Sponsors consistently cite limited internal understanding, insufficient analytical development documentation, and uncertainty about regulatory benefit as primary barriers; divergent health authority expectations across regions add further complexity. This perspective describes the scientific foundations of ECs for analytical procedures, synthesizes data from multiple surveys to characterize the current state of global implementation, and pairs practical challenges directly with scientific considerations. Particular attention is given to the untapped potential for generic drug developers, a community well-positioned to leverage prior knowledge, platform methods, and post-approval change volume to benefit from EC adoption. Written from the perspective of FDA analytical researchers, this paper aims to help bridge the persistent gap between laboratory rigor and dossier-ready EC documentation.

articles.title: Molecular Landscape of Inflammatory Bowel Disease: From Molecular Mechanisms to Emerging Pharmacological Strategies.
articles.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic inflammatory condition of the gastrointestinal tract, broadly classified into ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease, that affects millions of people worldwide. Despite significant advances in therapeutic options, including biologics, small-molecule drugs, and microbiota-targeted therapies, the aetiology of IBD remains incompletely understood. There is currently no curative treatment, and many patients experience suboptimal responses or severe treatment-related adverse effects. Increasing evidence suggests that IBD results from a complex interplay of genetic susceptibility, impaired epithelial barrier integrity, dysregulation of innate and adaptive immune responses and altered host-microbiome interactions. These disruptions trigger key inflammatory pathways and receptors, such as TNF receptors and IL-23R signalling, which sustain intestinal inflammation and contribute to disease severity and therapeutic resistance. This review summarises current understanding of IBD pathogenesis and highlights both established and emerging molecular targets. It also critically evaluates recent advances in drug discovery and targeted delivery strategies. By integrating mechanistic insights with translational approaches, this review aims to support the development of more effective, mechanism-driven, and personalised therapies for IBD.

articles.title: NKCC1 in Sepsis-Related Acute Lung Injury: Emerging Links to Macrophage-Neutrophil Crosstalk.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Sepsis-related acute lung injury (ALI) is a critical condition characterized by intense inflammation and damage to the lung tissue. Excessive activation of immune cells, particularly macrophages and neutrophils, is a key factor in the development of ALI. The sodium-potassium-chloride cotransporter 1 (NKCC1) plays a pivotal role in managing pulmonary fluid balance and inflammation and is critically involved in ALI. METHODS: A comprehensive literature review was conducted to evaluate studies examining macrophages, neutrophils, and NKCC1 in ALI, focusing on NKCC1 and its interactions with macrophages and neutrophils. RESULTS: Recognition of damage-associated or pathogen-associated molecular patterns by pattern recognition receptors on macrophages and neutrophils initiates downstream signaling cascades, including the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) and nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) pathways, which drive the production of proinflammatory mediators. The subsequent release of cytokines, including chemokines, promotes neutrophil recruitment to the lungs, where these neutrophils subsequently produce reactive oxygen species, proteases, and neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), thus amplifying inflammation and contributing to tissue injury. Excessive NET formation causes lung tissue injury, increases pulmonary vascular permeability, and disrupts gas exchange. During ALI, NKCC1 expression is elevated, which exacerbates lung inflammation and pulmonary edema. CONCLUSION: Sepsis-related ALI is characterized by excessive macrophage and neutrophil activation and activation of the MAPK and NF-κB pathways. Increased NKCC1 expression and activity contribute to pulmonary edema and inflammation in experimental ALI. However, the proposed role of NKCC1 in regulating macrophage-neutrophil interactions in sepsis-related ALI remains to be established.

articles.title: Why pH-responsive polymeric nanocarriers for doxorubicin have not yet achieved clinical translation: mechanistic insights and future directions.
articles.abstract: Doxorubicin (DOX) remains an important anthracycline chemotherapeutic agent for treating hematological and solid malignancies; however, its clinical application is severely constrained by cumulative dose-related cardiotoxicity and other systemic toxicities. pH-responsive polymeric nanocarriers have emerged as an encouraging approach to improve tumor-selective drug delivery by exploiting the slightly acidic tumor microenvironment for regulated DOX release. Despite extensive preclinical research, these nanocarriers have not yet achieved routine clinical use, emphasizing a persistent gap between laboratory success and clinical translation. This review scrutinizes the mechanistic principles underlying pH-responsive polymeric drug delivery and the interconnected biological, physicochemical, pharmacokinetic, manufacturing, and regulatory barriers responsible for translational failure. Particular attention is given to tumor heterogeneity, variable extracellular acidity, protein corona formation, rapid mononuclear phagocyte system clearance, restricted tumor penetration, the heterogeneous contribution of the enhanced permeability and retention effect, and the limited predictive value of conventional preclinical models. In contrast, clinically authorized liposomal doxorubicin formulations such as Doxil® and Myocet® demonstrate clinically meaningful changes in pharmacokinetics and reduced cardiotoxicity through stable liposomal encapsulation. Strategies including dual- and multi-stimuli-responsive systems, active targeting, biodegradable polymer architectures, artificial intelligence-assisted polymer design, companion diagnostics, and real-time theranostic monitoring are discussed to overcome current limitations. Collectively, this review provides a mechanistic framework for understanding persistent barriers to clinical translation and emphasizes design principles supporting more effective and clinically translatable DOX nanomedicines.

articles.title: Full mass spectrum background subtraction in LC-HRMS drug metabolite profiling: untargeted detection, integrated structural characterization, and applications.
articles.abstract: Over the past two decades, liquid chromatography-high-resolution mass spectrometry, coupled with targeted data-processing tools such as mass defect filtering, has become a principal platform for drug metabolite profiling and structural characterization. These approaches sensitively detect expected metabolites but may provide limited coverage of unexpected biotransformation products, particularly metabolites of emerging drug modalities and components of multicomponent traditional Chinese medicines) with difficult-to-predict masses, mass defects, or fragmentation behavior. Full mass spectrum background subtraction (FMS-BS) provides a complementary untargeted approach by directly comparing full-scan accurate-mass data from a test sample with data from an appropriate control. Removal of shared background ions retains drug-related components and generates clarified chromatograms and mass spectra for metabolite detection. These outputs help identify candidate metabolites for further MS/MS analysis and structural characterization. Because full-scan MS data are commonly acquired during LC-HRMS analysis in biotransformation studies, FMS-BS has the potential to serve as a general-purpose, prediction-independent data-processing tool without requiring major changes to existing analytical workflows. This Minireview critically evaluates the principles, strengths, limitations, and applications of FMS-BS relative to targeted and other untargeted LC-HRMS data-processing approaches. Applications span small molecules, cyclic peptides, oligonucleotide-based therapeutics, antibody-drug conjugate payload-containing components, protein adducts, and traditional Chinese medicines. FMS-BS can be used alone for untargeted data analysis or integrated with targeted processing approaches and sequence-based software for metabolite detection followed by structural characterization. As drug development moves toward increasingly complex modalities, integrating untargeted and targeted LC-HRMS data-processing approaches may provide broader and more complementary coverage of drug metabolites and related biotransformation products. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Full mass spectrum background subtraction (FMS-BS) is a prediction-independent data-processing technology for detecting drug-related components in full-scan LC-HRMS data. This first comprehensive review of FMS-BS systematically defines its principles, capabilities, limitations, and applications across small molecules, emerging therapeutic modalities, and TCMs. It highlights the integration of FMS-BS with targeted and sequence-based data processing to broaden metabolite detection and support structural characterization of increasingly complex drug modalities.

articles.title: Anxiolytic effects of cannabigerol: Hype or hope?
articles.abstract: Cannabigerol (CBG), a nonintoxicating phytocannabinoid derived from cannabigerolic acid, has gained increasing attention as a potential therapeutic agent for anxiety-related disorders and is widely marketed for stress reduction and emotional wellness. However, scientific evidence supporting these claims remains limited and inconsistent. In this review, we summarize the biosynthesis, pharmacokinetic properties, metabolism, and molecular targets of CBG, emphasizing its interactions with cannabinoid, serotonergic, α2-adrenergic, and transient receptor potential signaling pathways implicated in emotional regulation. We then applied a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses-style literature search strategy to critically evaluate the current evidence regarding the anxiolytic potential of CBG and identify factors that may explain divergent findings across studies. By integrating pharmacodynamic, pharmacokinetic, preclinical, and clinical evidence, we conclude that current data do not support classifying CBG as a consistently effective anxiolytic. Instead, available findings suggest that CBG acts as a context-dependent modulator of emotional behavior whose therapeutic potential remains to be established through pharmacokinetic-informed mechanistic studies and adequately powered clinical trials. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Cannabigerol (CBG) is increasingly promoted as a nonintoxicating anxiolytic despite limited and conflicting evidence supporting its efficacy. This review integrates pharmacokinetic, mechanistic, preclinical, and clinical findings to show that CBG produces context-dependent effects that vary according to exposure profile, biological state, and behavioral domain. These findings shift the field from asking whether CBG is anxiolytic to identifying the conditions under which CBG may meaningfully influence anxiety-related behavior.

articles.title: From VDR-associated transcriptional changes to monocyte differentiation impairment: an interpretive gap in PFAS immunotoxicity.
Comparative efficacy and safety of topical olopatadine formulations for allergic conjunctivitis: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Allergic conjunctivitis (AC) affects 15%-40% of the global population. Traditional network meta-analyses often group different formulations of olopatadine into a single node, obscuring concentration-dependent variations. This network meta-analysis evaluated the relative efficacy and safety of distinct olopatadine concentrations (0.1%, 0.2%, 0.77%) against other topical anti-allergic or anti-inflammatory agents. METHODS: Registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261375330), this study systematically searched major databases up to 1 May 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) on adults with AC. Interventions evaluated olopatadine formulations (0.1% BID, 0.2% QD, 0.77% QD) as independent nodes alongside 0.05% epinastine, 0.025% ketotifen, 0.25% alcaftadine, 1.5% bepotastine, 0.2% loteprednol etabonate, or placebo. Frequentist random-effects network meta-analyses were performed. RESULTS: Nineteen randomized controlled trials (RCTs) encompassing 2,745 patients (5,141 eyes) were analyzed. For ocular itching (18 RCTs), 0.77% olopatadine demonstrated superior efficacy among dual-acting agents (SUCRA = 80.7%), significantly outperforming epinastine and ketotifen. For conjunctival hyperemia (17 RCTs), 0.25% alcaftadine demonstrated the highest likelihood of efficacy (SUCRA = 66.5%), whereas among olopatadine formulations, only 0.2% significantly outperformed placebo (SUCRA = 47.4%). Subgroup analyses showed that 0.77% olopatadine and 0.25% alcaftadine were particularly effective against acute itching in conjunctival allergen challenge models. Safety assessments across 11 RCTs yielded wide confidence intervals due to data sparsity, precluding definitive tolerability rankings. Although trial data predominantly reported mild adverse events, external evidence highlights key long-term safety concerns, notably intraocular pressure elevation associated with extended topical corticosteroid therapy such as 0.2% loteprednol etabonate. CONCLUSION: Topical dual-acting agents demonstrate outcome-specific efficacy variations in allergic conjunctivitis management. Olopatadine 0.77% excels in pruritus control, whereas alcaftadine 0.25% provides the highest likelihood of hyperemia resolution. Clinical management should adopt a personalized step-ladder approach: utilizing potent once-daily dual-acting agents (0.77% olopatadine or 0.25% alcaftadine) as first-line therapy for acute or seasonal exposure. Short-term topical corticosteroids (such as 0.2% loteprednol etabonate) should be strictly reserved for severe natural exposure non-responsive to dual-acting agents, with mandatory intraocular pressure monitoring, before transitioning back to dual-acting maintenance.

articles.title: Natural compounds regulating MAPK-related signaling pathways: potential intervention strategies for gastric cancer.
articles.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) is a common malignant tumor of the digestive system, and its progression involves multiple molecular factors and signaling pathways. Dysregulation of mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK)-related signaling pathways is closely associated with the proliferation, invasion, metastasis, and drug resistance of GC. This review summarizes the major upstream factors associated with MAPK dysregulation, including Helicobacter pylori infection, genetic mutations, Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection, and epigenetic regulation. In addition, this review explores MAPK-related biological processes, including autophagy, oxidative stress, apoptosis, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), and cell cycle arrest. This paper focuses specifically on natural compounds capable of modulating ERK, JNK, and p38 MAPK-related signaling, as well as their interactions with other signaling networks, including PI3K/Akt, JAK/STAT3, and reactive oxygen species (ROS). Current evidence is primarily derived from preclinical studies; direct validation of target binding is limited, and significant gaps remain regarding pharmacokinetics, bioavailability, safety, and clinical translation. Therefore, further mechanistic and translational studies are needed to elucidate the therapeutic potential of natural compounds that modulate MAPK-related signaling pathways in GC.

articles.title: Reframing liquid biopsy microRNAs as functional readouts of Tumor-Microenvironment cross-talk.
articles.abstract: Liquid biopsy-associated microRNAs have been widely investigated as minimally invasive biomarkers for cancer detection, prognosis, and treatment monitoring. However, their clinical translation remains constrained by methodological variability, incomplete biological contextualization, and limited integration with therapeutic decision-making. This review proposes that extracellular microRNAs may be more informatively interpreted not only as passive indicators of tumor burden, but also as dynamic molecular readouts of tumor-microenvironment cross-talk, extracellular matrix remodeling, immune and stromal reprogramming, and pre-metastatic niche conditioning. We discuss how carrier-resolved profiling may refine the interpretation of circulating microRNAs by distinguishing extracellular vesicle-associated, Argonaute/ribonucleoprotein-bound, lipoprotein-associated, and other extracellular RNA fractions. Particular attention is given to competing endogenous RNA networks, microRNA-binding-site stoichiometry, and the mechanobiological regulation of extracellular vesicle release and microRNA cargo by matrix stiffness. We also examine the translational barriers that continue to limit clinical implementation, including pre-analytical variability, hemolysis, platelet contamination, extracellular vesicle purification, normalization bias, and insufficient prospective validation. Finally, we explore how liquid biopsy-derived RNA states could inform RNA-based therapeutics, biomimetic delivery strategies, and context-dependent theranostic approaches aimed at improving tumor-context specificity while reducing off-target toxicity. By integrating carrier identity, tumor ecosystem biology, RNA competition, mechanobiology, and therapeutic context, this review outlines a conceptual framework that may help guide the evolution of microRNA liquid biopsy from static biomarker discovery toward clinically actionable, network-aware precision oncology.

articles.title: Acipimox as a clinical pharmacology probe: A two-level bibliometric analysis of antilipolysis and bioenergetic readouts.
articles.abstract: Acipimox was introduced as a nicotinic acid analogue for lipid modification, but its later use has shifted towards experimental suppression of lipolysis in human metabolic studies. We examined whether this pattern reflects loss of drug identity or mechanism-constrained reuse of an established pharmacodynamic effect. Bibliographic records from PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus were harmonized into a frozen dataset of 863 records. A nested two-level framework defined a Broad Application Space (n = 428), within which a stricter Drug-Identity Core (n = 239) was identified. Bibliometric mapping was interpreted alongside landmark pharmacological studies to preserve a clinical pharmacology perspective. The 428-record Broad Application Space comprised 239 Drug-Identity Core records and 189 Broad-only application/probe records. The nested Core remained centred on lipid lowering, tolerability, lipolytic-enzyme regulation and suppression of free fatty acid availability, whereas the additional Broad-only literature extended into insulin sensitivity, endocrine physiology, skeletal-muscle fuel handling and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide- and mitochondrial-linked metabolic readouts. The pivotal pharmacological signal was not a complete transformation of acipimox into a mitochondrial drug, but recurrent experimental reuse of receptor-linked antilipolysis. Acipimox illustrates how an older compound can retain value when a well-characterized pharmacodynamic action is reused as a probe of lipid substrate availability, substrate competition and selected bioenergetic readouts. Such use requires explicit attention to timing, rebound non-esterified fatty acids and tissue context.

articles.title: Bioequivalence of two formulations of amitriptyline hydrochloride tablets in healthy Chinese subjects under fasting and fed conditions.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The study evaluated the bioequivalence and tolerability of a generic amitriptyline hydrochloride tablet compared to the reference product in healthy Chinese subjects under both fasting and postprandial conditions to support its marketing authorization. METHODS: A single-center, open-label, randomized, single-dose, two-period, two-sequence crossover study was conducted. Eligible subjects took a single 25 mg dose of the generic or reference product per cycle in random order. Plasma drug concentrations were detected by LC-MS/MS and the bioequivalence of the two formulations was assessed through key pharmacokinetic parameters (Cmax, AUC0-t, and AUC0-∞) of amitriptyline. Adverse events were continuously monitored throughout the trial. RESULTS: The 90% confidence intervals (CIs) for the geometric mean ratios (GMRs) of Cmax, AUC0-t, and AUC0-∞ between the two products fell within the 80-125% range under both fasting and postprandial conditions. Our study indicated that food intake increases systemic exposure to amitriptyline without affecting Tmax. Both formulations were well tolerated, with predominantly mild adverse events and no severe or fatal events. CONCLUSION: The generic amitriptyline hydrochloride tablets by Changzhou Siyao Pharmaceuticals Co., Ltd. were bioequivalent to the reference formulation by Sandoz Inc. with comparable tolerability. TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered at www.chinadrugtrials.org.cn under the registration number CTR20212242 (November 2, 2021).

articles.title: Artificial intelligence support for the prediction and management of drug-drug interactions.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Drug-drug interactions (DDIs) are a preventable cause of adverse drug events (ADEs), yet conventional interaction-checking tools are hampered by incomplete knowledge, poor concordance, and clinically unusable alert burdens. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly utilized to strengthen multiple stages of the DDI pathway. AREAS COVERED: This narrative review synthesizes literature identified through searches conducted between 15 July and 20 October 2026. It examines how machine learning (ML) predicts novel drug interactions from molecular structure and knowledge graphs; how natural language processing (NLP) and large language models (LLMs) identify and extract interactions from the literature, drug labels, and pharmacovigilance data; and how AI can make clinical decision support context-aware and support medication review. It also integrates mechanistic physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling and individualized patient-level risk prediction. EXPERT OPINION: Prediction models achieve impressive benchmark accuracy but frequently underperform in realistic, cold-start settings; LLMs detect interactions with high sensitivity but show poor severity calibration and persistent hallucination. The near-term value of AI lies less in autonomous prediction than in curating knowledge, personalizing alerts, and augmenting clinician judgment. Rigorous external validation, interpretability, and regulatory clarity are prerequisites for clinical adoption.

articles.title: RETRACTED: Shafiq et al. Development and Optimization of Tamarind Gum-β-Cyclodextrin-g-Poly(Methacrylate) pH-Responsive Hydrogels for Sustained Delivery of Acyclovir. Pharmaceuticals 2022, 15, 1527.

articles.title: Psychedelic experience intensity during ketamine treatment and antidepressant outcomes.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Ketamine is an effective antidepressant, but the role of acute subjective effects in treatment response remains unclear. Prior studies rely largely on dissociation measures focused on adverse events, which may not capture broader effects across multiple phenomenological domains. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether subjective psychedelic intensity during ketamine treatment, considered beyond an adverse-event framework, is associated with antidepressant outcomes. METHODS: In this retrospective longitudinal cohort study, 3,637 adults with moderate-to-severe depression received up to 4 doses of sublingual ketamine over 4 weeks within a telehealth-supported treatment program. Subjective effects were assessed using the Mindbloom Psychedelic Intensity (MPI) scale, a novel 5-item measure capturing emotional, cognitive, physical, visual, and auditory effects. Primary outcomes included end-of-treatment change in Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) scores, clinically significant change, and treatment response trajectories. Pre-registered analyses evaluated whether MPI scores at the midpoint of treatment were associated with antidepressant outcomes. RESULTS: Higher subjective intensity scores at 2 weeks were associated with greater reductions in depression severity at 4 weeks, increased likelihood of clinically significant change, and greater likelihood of membership in an improvement trajectory, independent of dose and other covariates. CONCLUSIONS: Subjective intensity of the ketamine experience was robustly associated with antidepressant outcomes. These findings suggest that subjective drug effects represent a clinically meaningful correlate of treatment response and highlight the importance of assessments designed to capture first-person experiences with ketamine, with implications for future mechanistic research and clinical care.

articles.title: Quality by design development of folic acid-engineered berberine nanoliposomes for targeted triple-negative breast cancer therapy.
articles.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains one of the most challenging breast cancer subtypes due to the lack of actionable molecular targets and the systemic toxicity associated with standard chemotherapy. Berberine chloride (BBR), a plant-derived isoquinoline alkaloid, exhibits promising anticancer activity; however, its poor solubility and limited bioavailability restrict therapeutic utility. Therefore, liposomal encapsulation was explored to improve BBR delivery, while folic acid functionalization was introduced to enhance preferential interaction with folate receptor-expressing TNBC cells. In this study, folic acid-decorated nanoliposomes were developed to enhance the targeted delivery of BBR to TNBC cells. BBR-loaded liposomes and folic acid-functionalized liposomes were prepared using the solvent injection method and optimized through a Quality-by-Design (QbD) framework. The optimized folate-modified formulation showed a mean particle size of 168.3 nm with an entrapment efficiency of 41.8%, while non-targeted liposomes exhibited a smaller size (95.6 nm) and slightly higher entrapment loading (47.5%). Both systems provided sustained drug release over 72 h, with folate-decorated liposomes demonstrating a more controlled release pattern. Cytotoxicity studies in MDA-MB-231 cells following 24 h of treatment revealed significantly enhanced antiproliferative activity of folate-functionalized nanoliposomes (IC50 = 24.72 μM) compared to non-targeted liposomes and free BBR. Increased intracellular reactive oxygen species generation following folate-mediated delivery suggested oxidative stress-associated cytotoxicity. Importantly, preliminary safety evaluation using Drosophila melanogaster confirmed the biocompatibility of the liposomal formulations. Overall, folic acid-decorated nanoliposomes substantially improve the therapeutic efficacy of berberine and offer a rational nanocarrier approach for TNBC management.

articles.title: Lipid-lowering, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory effects of Erythrina speciosa and its triterpenoids in acute dyslipidemia.
articles.abstract: Dyslipidemia is a health concern that contributes to metabolic and cardiovascular complications. The present study evaluated the anti-dyslipidemic potential of the chloroform fraction of Erythrina speciosa leaves and its isolated constituents, with particular emphasis on lipid regulation, redox balance, and inflammatory mediators. Chromatographic separation of the chloroform fraction led to the isolation of five triterpenoids, reported here for the first time from E. speciosa. The biological activity was assessed in a poloxamer-407-induced acute hyperlipidemia model in rats. Treatment with the chloroform fraction, isolated compounds, or atorvastatin significantly attenuated elevations in serum total cholesterol and triglycerides and improved low-density lipoprotein-cholesterol (LDL-C). These effects were accompanied by restoration of lipoprotein lipase (LPL) activity, upregulation of hepatic LDL receptor (LDL-R), downregulation of fatty acid synthase (FAS), and suppression of 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase (HMG-CoA) reductase. Moreover, E. speciosa and its triterpenoids markedly alleviated oxidative stress and inflammation, as evidenced by reduced malondialdehyde (MDA), nitric oxide (NO), nuclear factor-kappaB (NF-κB) p65, tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, and interleukin (IL)- 1β and enhanced antioxidants. Molecular docking provided supportive computational evidence by predicting favorable binding interactions of the isolated compounds with NF-κB p65, LDL-R PCSK9 binding domain, and FAS. In conclusion, E. speciosa and its triterpenoids are promising candidates for the management of dyslipidemia and related inflammatory and oxidative disturbances.

articles.title: Machine learning pipeline for secretome biomarker discovery in colorectal cancer: from single-cell transcriptomics to functional validation.
articles.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) requires robust biomarkers and therapeutic targets. This study aimed to identify secretome-associated genes with diagnostic, prognostic, and tumor-suppressive relevance in CRC, focusing on GUCA2B (uroguanylin). We integrated single-cell transcriptomics, pseudobulk differential expression, machine learning (ML), multi-omics, and in vitro functional assays (HCT-116 cells). ML consensus feature selection across four algorithms identified 20 shared features from 850 downregulated genes; eight genes, including GUCA2B, were selected by all four models, forming the finalized signature. GUCA2B was markedly reduced in CRC epithelium. A frozen eight-gene logistic model showed an apparent (training-set) AUC of 0.998 in TCGA-COADREAD and maintained discrimination in three independent cohorts (AUC = 0.881-0.974). Reduced GUCA2B expression correlated with adverse survival, promoter hypermethylation, and altered immune infiltration. In vitro, GUCA2B restoration induced intrinsic apoptosis (increased BAX, decreased BCL2), reduced viability, and impaired migration; because GC-C/cGMP dependence was not tested, these effects constitute receptor-mechanism-agnostic proof of concept. In conclusion, GUCA2B represents a candidate epithelial-restricted CRC biomarker and tumor-suppressive gene. While the frozen multi-gene model shows promise for diagnostic stratification and GUCA2B restoration demonstrates preliminary tumor-suppressive activity, the small discovery set (n = 23 pseudobulk samples), moderate feature-selection stability, and single-cell-line validation necessitate cautious interpretation. Prospective clinical validation and in vivo multi-model studies are required before diagnostic or therapeutic application.

articles.title: Inhaled Glucocorticoids During Pregnancy: A Population-Level Drug Utilization Study in Denmark From 2001 to 2023.
articles.abstract: We investigated trends of inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) use among pregnant women in Denmark from 2001 to 2023 using aggregated data from the Danish Health Data Authority, where recorded prescription redemptions in the National Prescription Register are linked to pregnancies recorded in the Danish Medical Birth Registry. Use of combination preparations (ICS and beta2-agonists) increased substantially (from 1.3 to 21 per 1000 pregnant women), corresponding to a 16-fold increase, while use of single-agent preparations (ICS) decreased gradually (from 17 to 11 per 1000 pregnant women). Combination preparations became more prevalent than single-agent preparations in 2020 among pregnant women, reflecting changes in treatment guidelines and recommendations in 2019. ICS use was higher before than during pregnancy in 2001 (22 vs. 18 per 1000 women) but lower before than during pregnancy in 2023 (30 vs. 32 per 1000 women), with the pattern reversing in 2015. Use during pregnancy was highest among the oldest women (≥ 40 years), with some variation over time, while it fluctuated substantially among the youngest women (≤ 19 years) and increased more steadily among women aged 20-39 years. Overall, our results highlight changes in ICS use among pregnant women that are well aligned with national and international asthma guidelines.

articles.title: Population pharmacokinetics and exposure-response analysis of acalabrutinib in patients with untreated mantle cell lymphoma in the ECHO trial.
articles.abstract: AIMS: The phase 3 ECHO trial demonstrated superior progression-free survival (PFS) with acalabrutinib plus bendamustine-rituximab (BR) versus placebo plus BR in treatment-naive (TN) mantle cell lymphoma (MCL). This analysis characterizes the pharmacokinetic (PK) profile of acalabrutinib and ACP-5862 (active metabolite) when administered with BR and evaluates exposure-response (efficacy/safety) relationships based on ECHO data. METHODS: In ECHO, patients aged ≥65 years with TN MCL received BR plus acalabrutinib or placebo. Acalabrutinib (100 mg twice daily) or placebo was administered at study start until progressive disease or unacceptable toxicity. A pooled population PK analysis dataset included 975 patients for acalabrutinib and 580 patients for ACP-5862 from ECHO plus 10 clinical trials. Exposure-response analyses examined associations between exposure and PFS, best overall response (BOR), and adverse events (AEs) from ECHO.
