RESULTS: Population PK analysis showed that demographics (age, body weight, sex, ethnicity, race) and other intrinsic factors (mild or moderate renal impairment; mild or moderate hepatic impairment) had no meaningful effect on acalabrutinib/ACP-5862 exposure. No impact of co-administration with BR was observed on PK exposure. Exposure-efficacy analyses of ECHO data showed a flat relationship between acalabrutinib/ACP-5862 exposure and PFS and BOR. Exposure-safety analyses of ECHO data showed no clinically meaningful correlation between acalabrutinib/ACP-5862 exposure and selected safety outcomes (grade ≥3 AEs and events of clinical interest, AEs leading to dose modifications). CONCLUSION: This analysis supports a fixed 100 mg twice daily acalabrutinib dose, in combination with BR, as well-tolerated and efficacious in treatment of patients with TN MCL.

articles.title: Mass balance and metabolite profiles in humans of ACT001, a novel sesquiterpene lactone derivative, using 14C-radiolabelled techniques.
articles.abstract: AIMS: ACT001, a novel sesquiterpene lactone derivative, is effective against treating glioblastoma multiforme and other diseases. This study aims to investigate its metabolic and excretion characteristics. METHODS: A single oral dose of 600 mg/200 μCi [14C]ACT001 was administered to six healthy subjects. Blood, urine and fecal samples were collected and measured for total radioactivity (TRA), ACT001 and its main metabolite (monomethylamine micheliolide, MA-MCL). The safety was also assessed. RESULTS: The mean elimination half-life (t1/2) of TRA, of TRA, ACT001 and MA-MCL were 33.7 h, 3.16 h, and 8.45 h, respectively. ACT001 and MA-MCL accounted for 14.49% and 30.50% of TRA, respectively. In addition, radiochromatographic profiling confirmed no other individual metabolite exceeded 2% of total peak area. The individual ratios of total radioactivity in whole blood relative to plasma ranged from 0.330 to 0.827. The primary excretion route of ACT001 was urine (accounting for 90.08% ± 1.16% of dose), with a small amount excreted in faeces (accounting for 7.30% ± 0.66% of dose), resulting in a total excretion rate of 97.39% ± 0.93%. Metabolites represented more than 80% of urinary excretion. The main metabolic pathways involved demethylation, oxidation, and dealkylation to form micheliolide and glucuronidation or cysteine conjugation of related metabolites. CONCLUSIONS: [14C]ACT001 was rapidly absorbed but slowly eliminated, as reflected by the longer elimination t1/2 of TRA (33.7 h) vs. ACT001 (3.16 h) and MA-MCL (8.45 h). The overall mass balance was nearly complete. ACT001 and MA-MCL were the primary circulating compounds. Demethylated metabolites were the primary substances excreted in urine and faeces.

articles.title: Longan polysaccharides protect against DSS-induced colitis and suppress NLRP12-associated PANoptosis-related signaling.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: The dried aril of longan (Dimocarpus longan Lour.) is used in traditional Chinese medicine to nourish blood and tonify the heart and spleen. Longan polysaccharides (LP) have reported immunomodulatory and anti-inflammatory activities, but the evidence for their effects on inflammatory cell-death pathways in colitis remain limited. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study was designed to evaluate the protective effects of LP in a chronic relapsing dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis and explore associated changes in NLRP12 expression and selected inflammatory cell-death markers. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Male ICR mice received LP (100, 200, or 400 mg/kg) before and during three DSS exposure/recovery cycles. Disease activity, histopathology, junctional-protein expression, exploratory transcriptomics, immunofluorescence, Western blotting, and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) were assessed. RESULTS: LP dose-dependently reduced DAI, colon shortening, histological injury, and goblet-cell loss, while increasing the tissue expression of junctional proteins. Transcriptomic candidates were confirmed at protein level, with lower NLRP12, CLEC7A and IL-1A after LP-H. LP-H reduced GSDMD-N, cleaved caspase-1, IL-18, the mature IL-1beta species, and cleaved caspase-3 by Western blotting. Besides, LP-H significantly reduced p-MLKL/MLKL. TEM showed attenuation of epithelial and mitochondrial ultrastructural injury. These findings identify suppression of NLRP12-associated pyroptotic, apoptotic and necroptotic signaling as a feature of LP-mediated protection. CONCLUSION: Under a preventive dosing regimen, LP attenuated chronic relapsing DSS colitis and suppressed NLRP12-associated PANoptosis-related signaling, with coordinate down-regulation of markers of pyroptosis, apoptosis and necroptosis.

articles.title: Water ingress as the master variable in polymeric delivery Devices: Constituent Thermodynamics, matrix Relaxation, and the Two-Region diffusion of bioactive molecules.
articles.abstract: A polymeric delivery device is usually stored as a glass and does nothing until water enters it. This review takes water ingress as the primary object of study for physically entangled, un-crosslinked hydrophilic matrices, with the bioactive at infinite dilution. First, the Flory-Huggins free energy of the water-polymer-bioactive mixture fixes the water activity, the osmotic driving force, the Darken factor and the partition coefficient: it supplies driving forces, necessary for a rate but not sufficient. Second, the rate comes from coupling penetrant diffusion to matrix relaxation. Water converts a glassy pharmaceutical polymer to a rubber at a critical content set by its dry glass transition, and because viscosity falls exponentially with water content, the sorption profile sharpens into a front whose width scales inversely with a water Péclet number. Third, and centrally, the front meets the bioactive in one of two topologies. In a glassy matrix it gates release in series with gel-layer diffusion, and the exponent m of the empirical power law F ∝ tm falls from 0.99 to 0.50 as the front speeds up; in a rubbery matrix, surface erosion acts in parallel with diffusion, and the exponent rises from 0.50 to 0.92. The branches cross near 0.67, so an exponent alone does not identify a mechanism: the dry-state glass transition fixes the topology, and the fitting protocol must be stated, since defensible conventions differ by up to 0.075. Geometry enters through a shape factor varying by at most a half across common shapes, whereas size changes the governing rate ratio by orders of magnitude. Applied without fitting, the framework predicts a poly(ethylene oxide) slab to within 0.09 in the exponent and brackets a hydroxypropyl methylcellulose disc whose front is too diffuse to act as a gate.

articles.title: Impact of coprocessed excipient composition on fluid bed processed orodispersible minitablets.
articles.abstract: Orodispersible minitablets (ODMTs) represent a versatile dosage form with a well-documented utility in literature across diverse patient populations. The majority of emerging active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) belong to the Class II Biopharmaceutics Classification System (BCS), necessitating particle size reduction to increase the surface area and thereby enhance dissolution. Micronisation, while effective, adversely affects powder flowability, which is critical for blend uniformity and consistent die filling during minitablet manufacture. Therefore, a micronized API requires a granulation step. In this study, fluid bed processing was selected as it offers the particular advantage of producing porous, free-flowing particles of controlled particle size distribution that support consistent die filling. Additionally, fluid bed processing supports blend uniformity, which later translates into uniform tablet content. Previous studies on the preparation of ODTs and minitablets for a poorly soluble API demonstrated the advantage of using co-processed excipients (CPEs). Thus, processing CPEs that already include the filler, binder and superdisintegrants via fluid bed processing presents further advantages, as it eliminates multiple blend conditioning steps and requires only lubrication prior to compression. This also offers the possibility to operate at lower temperatures. Aqueous fluid bed processing is environmentally preferable to solvent-based alternatives; however, it carries an inherent risk of premature activation of the superdisintegrants within the CPE during processing, with potential disintegration failure of the produced ODMTs. This study systematically investigates the factors governing the success of aqueous fluid bed processing, with particular focus on CPE composition and its physicochemical properties. A stepwise approach is taken, progressing from CPEs of simple composition to those of greater complexity, while evaluating the influence of the material properties, including morphology, particle size distribution and moisture sorption behaviour on both the process dynamics and the critical product attributes of the final tablets. The findings demonstrate that the CPE composition, particle size distribution and hygroscopicity are critical determinants of the process outcomes. CPEs containing croscarmellose withstand aqueous fluid bed processing and yield ODMTs with adequate quality attributes, whereas CPEs containing crospovidone and broad span are susceptible to process failure and the resulting ODMT batches fail to meet critical product attribute specifications.

articles.title: Neuroprotective effects of ropinirole against nicotine- and ethanol-induced cognitive impairment, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and neurodegenerative alterations in rats.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Adolescence is a critical period of brain development during which exposure to addictive substances may adversely affect cognitive function and neuronal plasticity. Combined nicotine and ethanol exposure may contribute to persistent cognitive impairment through disturbances in oxidative balance, inflammatory signaling, and hippocampal function. However, the potential effects of pharmacological interventions targeting these alterations after exposure remain insufficiently characterized. Given the previously reported neuroprotective properties of ropinirole, this study investigated whether post-exposure treatment with this dopamine D2/D3 receptor agonist could attenuate cognitive deficits and associated hippocampal biochemical alterations in rats subjected to adolescent nicotine-ethanol co-exposure. METHODS: Male Wistar rats were exposed to nicotine (2 mg/kg/day, intraperitoneally) and ethanol (20% v/v in drinking water) during adolescence (postnatal days 21-48). Following the exposure period, animals received oral ropinirole at doses of 5, 10, or 20 mg/kg/day for three weeks. Spatial learning and memory and recognition memory were assessed using the Morris water maze and novel object recognition tests, respectively. Hippocampal biochemical assessments included malondialdehyde (MDA), nitrite, total thiol content, superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase, tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-10 (IL-10), brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), acetylcholinesterase (AChE), and amyloid-β (Aβ). RESULTS: Nicotine-ethanol co-exposure significantly impaired spatial learning, memory retention, and recognition memory, accompanied by increased hippocampal MDA, nitrite, TNF-α, AChE activity, and Aβ levels, together with reduced antioxidant capacity, IL-10, and BDNF expression. Post-exposure ropinirole treatment improved performance in the behavioral tests and attenuated several of the associated biochemical alterations. The 20 mg/kg dose generally showed the most pronounced effects among the doses tested; however, a formal dose-response relationship was not established. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that ropinirole exerts neuroprotective effects against adolescent nicotine-ethanol-induced cognitive impairment through the modulation of oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, cholinergic dysfunction, neurotrophic signaling, and amyloid-related pathways. These results provide preliminary evidence supporting dopaminergic modulation as a potential strategy for mitigating substance-associated cognitive dysfunction, although further mechanistic and translational studies are necessary.

articles.title: Exercise improves endothelium-dependent H2S-mediated vasodilation in ovariectomized rats via a COX-dependent mechanism.
articles.abstract: 17β-estradiol (E2) stimulates the production of nitric oxide (NO) and hydrogen sulfide (H2S). Although physical exercise effectively enhances NO-mediated vasodilation under estrogen-deficient conditions, the role of H2S in this context is not yet fully understood. We investigated the effect of exercise on H2S-mediated dilation in the thoracic aorta of ovariectomized rats. Female Wistar rats were randomly divided into the following groups: Sham + Sedentary (SS), Sham + Exercise (SE), Ovariectomy + Sedentary (OS), and Ovariectomy + Exercise (OE). After eight weeks of exercise, vascular reactivity was assessed. NO and reactive oxygen species (ROS) were measured using DAF-2 and DHE probes, respectively. The OS group showed reduced H2S-mediated vasodilation; however, this response was significantly improved after exercise. Sodium hydrosulfide (NaHS) produced similar effects on vascular reactivity. Endothelial removal abolished the differences in exercise-induced improvement in H2S-mediated vasodilation. In addition, inhibition of NO synthesis did not prevent the exercise-induced enhancement of H2S-mediated vasodilation in the OS and OE groups, indicating a NO-independent mechanism. In contrast, cyclooxygenase (COX) inhibition abolished the exercise-induced improvement in H2S-mediated vasodilation. Exercise also increased NO production and reduced ROS generation. Our results demonstrate that exercise improves endothelium-dependent vasodilation through H2S formation via a COX-dependent mechanism in ovariectomized rats.

articles.title: HIF-1α deficiency limits hepatocellular carcinoma progression and modulates tyrosine kinase inhibitor responses.
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by extensive intratumoral hypoxia, which influences tumor progression and therapeutic response. Although tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) such as sorafenib and regorafenib represent key systemic treatments for advanced HCC, their clinical benefit is frequently limited by intrinsic or acquired resistance. Hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) 1α plays a central role in mediating adaptive responses that promote survival, metabolic plasticity, and treatment failure under hypoxia. In this study, we investigated the contribution of HIF-1α to TKI responsiveness using complementary in vitro and in vivo HCC models. HIF1A knockout (KO) was generated in Huh-7 and PLC/PRF/5 cells, which were exposed to CoCl2-induced hypoxia-mimicking conditions and treated with sorafenib or regorafenib. Cell viability, proliferation, migration and clonogenic capacity were assessed. Orthotopic murine xenograft models were used to evaluate tumor growth and therapeutic response in vivo. HIF1A deficiency was associated with reduced proliferative and clonogenic capacity, impaired wound closure and alterations in hypoxia-responsive pathways, including HIF-1α, HIF-2α, and BNIP3 signaling. Genotype-dependent responses to sorafenib and regorafenib were identified, revealing distinct effects across cell lines and functional endpoints. Importantly, HIF1A KO tumors exhibited significantly lower tumor-associated bioluminescence before treatment initiation and reduced tumor burden at the experimental endpoint. TKI treatment was also associated with reductions in tumor growth and proliferation, highlighting the contribution of HIF-1α signaling to tumor progression and treatment-associated responses. Collectively, these findings identify HIF-1α as an important regulator of HCC progression and support further investigation of the hypoxia-HIF-1α axis as a potential therapeutic target in HCC.

articles.title: Fam20C knockdown restrains glioma progression and potentiates temozolomide sensitivity by disrupting DNA damage repair.
articles.abstract: Gliomas are the most frequent intrinsic tumors of the central nervous system, featuring aggressive invasion, frequent recurrence and poor prognosis. Routine surgical resection, radiotherapy and chemotherapy have shown limited efficacy in improving cure rates or prolonging patient survival, suggesting an urgent need to identify novel prognostic biomarkers and druggable molecular targets for glioma. The family with sequence similarity 20, member C (Fam20C), a Golgi protein kinase governing phosphorylation of secreted proteins, was reported to be dysregulated in multiple malignancies. Herein, we found aberrantly elevated Fam20C expression in glioma tissues, and high Fam20C expression correlates with disease progression and predicts unfavorable clinical outcomes of glioma patients. Functional assays demonstrated that Fam20C knockdown markedly suppresses malignant proliferation, migration, and invasion of glioma cells. Mechanistically, Fam20C knockdown impairs ATM/ATR-mediated DNA damage repair and leads to intracellular DNA damage accumulation. Importantly, knockdown of Fam20C synergistically potentiates the anti-tumor efficacy of temozolomide (TMZ) upon combined administration. Moreover, the small-molecule Fam20C inhibitor compound 5 k synergizes with TMZ to suppress glioma cell proliferation and migration, and to induce apoptosis. Collectively, our findings establish Fam20C as a promising therapeutic target for glioma, and pharmacological blockade of Fam20C represents a viable translational strategy warranting further investigation to enhance anti-glioma effects.

articles.title: Upregulation of PGC-1α attenuates obesity-exacerbated myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury by restoring mitochondrial dynamics.
articles.abstract: Compared to normal individuals, obese individuals demonstrate exacerbated myocardial ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury and higher mortality, despite comparable baseline cardiac function. The underlying mechanisms may involve obesity-induced pathophysiological changes-particularly energy metabolism dysregulation and mitochondrial dysfunction-which impair the ability of cardiomyocytes to withstand I/R injury, thereby increasing myocardial susceptibility. Mitochondria, serving as the central hub of energy metabolism, are critically regulated by peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1-alpha (PGC-1α), a master regulator of mitochondrial biogenesis and metabolic homeostasis. However, the role of PGC-1α in the increased susceptibility of obese myocardium to I/R injury remains unclear. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the mechanisms through which obesity exacerbates myocardial vulnerability to I/R injury, with a specific focus on the role of PGC-1α and mitochondrial dysfunction, to facilitate the development of innovative therapeutic strategies for mitigating I/R injury and improving clinical outcomes in obese patients. C57BL/6J mice were fed a high-fat diet (HFD) for 25 consecutive weeks to establish an obesity model, while control mice received a normal chow diet (NCD). After dietary intervention, control and obese subgroups underwent I/R surgery. In vitro, H9c2 cells were treated with palmitic acid (PA) for 12 h in the presence or absence of PGC-1α overexpression, followed by anoxia/reoxygenation (A/R). Pre-I/R or A/R, cardiac function and cell viability showed no significant differences between obese and control groups. Post-I/R or A/R, the obese group demonstrated markedly worsened cardiac function, enlarged infarct size and reduced cell survival. This was accompanied by elevated mitochondrial and total reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, impaired antioxidant capacity (reduced superoxide dismutase (SOD) and glutathione peroxidase (GSH-Px) activity, increased malondialdehyde (MDA)), loss of mitochondrial membrane potential and enhanced mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP) opening-collectively indicating obesity significantly exacerbates I/R injury. Additionally, obese myocardium exhibited downregulated PGC-1α expression, reduced protein levels of nuclear respiratory factor 1 (NRF1) and mitochondrial transcription factor A (TFAM), abnormal mitochondrial dynamics (decreased mitofusin 2 (MFN2), increased dynamin-related protein 1 (DRP1)) and reduced adenosine triphosphate (ATP) production. Crucially, PGC-1α upregulation ameliorated mitochondrial dysfunction and thus attenuated I/R injury. These findings demonstrate that obesity exacerbates myocardial I/R injury through a key mechanism involving PGC-1α downregulation-induced mitochondrial dysfunction, which ultimately enhances cardiac susceptibility to I/R damage.

articles.title: Structure-guided intrinsic stabilization enhances apparent systemic persistence of thymosin α1 while preserving immunomodulatory function.
articles.abstract: Short therapeutic peptides are often limited by rapid systemic clearance and insufficient in vivo persistence. Although formulation- and carrier-based approaches can improve delivery, intrinsic sequence optimization remains underexplored. Using thymosin α1 (Tα-1) as a clinically validated model, we applied structure-guided intrinsic stabilization to improve apparent systemic persistence while preserving context-dependent immunomodulatory function. An AlphaFold-derived comparative scaffold, FoldX single-site scanning, and DUET cross-validation identified D15 and E27 as stability-permissive engineering sites. D15M showed the most consistent overall improvement, whereas E27R supported E27 as a second optimization site. Both variants retained native-like structural features, resisted serum-associated degradation, and showed prolonged apparent systemic persistence after both subcutaneous and intravenous administration. These gains were accompanied by preserved biological activity in immunosuppressed mice, a tumor xenograft model, murine and human macrophage systems, and donor-derived peripheral blood mononuclear cells. The optimized variants maintained the context-dependent immunomodulatory profile of native Tα-1 rather than producing a broad constitutive increase in intrinsic activity. These findings support structure-guided intrinsic stabilization as a complementary strategy for improving the developability and systemic performance of short therapeutic peptides without compromising biological function.

articles.title: CERS2-mediated very-long-chain ceramide accumulation drives lipophagy impairment in entrectinib-induced nephrotoxicity.
articles.abstract: Entrectinib, a blood-brain barrier-penetrant multi-target tyrosine kinase inhibitor, has demonstrated substantial clinical value in a variety of solid malignancies driven by NTRK, ROS1, or ALK gene fusions, particularly in patients with intracranial metastasis. However, with the expanding clinical use of entrectinib, the risk of entrectinib-associated nephrotoxicity has increasingly emerged. At present, the molecular mechanisms underlying this toxicity remain poorly understood, and effective predictive and interventional strategies are still lacking, which may limit its long-term safe application. Here, we showed that entrectinib (120 and 240 mg/kg) exposure induced marked renal dysfunction and tubular injury in mice, coupled with aberrant lipid droplet accumulation and lipid peroxidation-dependent apoptosis in renal tubular epithelial cells (RTECs). Mechanistically, 4 µM entrectinib triggered a marked upregulation of ceramide synthase 2 (CERS2), thereby promoting the abnormal accumulation of the very-long-chain ceramide Cer d18:1/22:0 in HK-2 cells. Further investigation revealed that Cer d18:1/22:0 disrupted lysosomal membrane integrity and impaired lysosomal degradative capacity, consequently blocking the lysosomal degradation of lipid droplets through lipophagy. The resulting impairment of lipophagic flux led to defective lipid droplet clearance and sustained intracellular lipid overload, ultimately triggering lipid peroxidation and lipotoxic apoptosis, thereby driving entrectinib-induced nephrotoxicity. Together, our finding elucidates the CERS2-Cer d18:1/22:0 axis as a key mediator of entrectinib-induced lysosomal dysfunction, lipophagic flux impairment, and lipotoxic apoptosis in RTECs. Collectively, these findings offer a mechanistic rationale for the development of targeted interventions against entrectinib-related nephrotoxicity, potentially guiding clinical strategies to improve treatment safety.

articles.title: Transcriptomic and metabolomic remodeling in HepG2 cells during continuous PFOA exposure.
articles.abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), a persistent environmental contaminant, is associated with hepatic metabolic dysfunction, yet the molecular consequences of sustained low-concentration exposure remain poorly characterized. Here, we used a serial-passage HepG2 cell model under continuous 8 μM PFOA exposure and integrated RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) with targeted metabolomics to compare cells at the first (G1, 48 h) and seventh (G7, 14 d) serial passages. PFOA did not affect cell viability at 48 h but induced clear transcriptomic and metabolomic divergence from controls. At G1, 255 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and 53 differential smetabolites were identified, with enrichment in nucleotide metabolism, central carbon metabolism, lipid pathways, and ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters. At G7, 2102 DEGs and 74 differential metabolites were identified, with enrichment in glycolysis/gluconeogenesis, amino acid and one‑carbon metabolism, glycerolipid metabolism, and mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) signaling. Cross-stage comparisons revealed stage-dependent differences in shared metabolites and representative genes. Joint pathway analysis highlighted glycerolipid metabolism as a persistently perturbed node, whereas central carbon metabolism became increasingly prominent at G7. A biochemically constrained gene-metabolite network identified five candidate association axes preferentially detected at G7: fructose 1,6-bisphosphate (F1,6BP)-ALDOC, F1,6BP-PFKL, F1,6BP-PFKP, inosine-NT5E, and nicotinamide-SIRT7, suggesting a distinct metabolic state involving glycolytic regulation, lipid homeostasis, purine metabolism, and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+)-dependent signaling. Collectively, this study provides an integrative multi-omics framework for PFOA hepatotoxicity and identifies candidate molecular axes for functional validation.

articles.title: Assessing adenovirus structural integrity and stability through analytical ultracentrifugation and supporting biophysical methods.
articles.abstract: Adenoviruses (AdV) are used as vectors for gene therapy and for vaccination, such as the COVID-19 vaccines AD26.COV2.S (AdV1) and ChAdOx1-S (AdV2). To develop a platform of methods for AdV characterization, we used untreated and thermally stressed samples. During heating ramps, nanoDSF/DLS detects first structural changes accompanied by aggregation for AdV1 and AdV2 at 50°C. SYBR green-enhanced DSF reveals an increased dye-accessibility of viral DNA within this temperature range, suggesting a loss of structural integrity of the capsid. By introducing the relative ratio of initial fluorescence to maximum fluorescence intensity at the transition point, we derive a numerical value reflecting the extent of heat-induced change. In heat-stressed samples also negative-staining transmission electron microscopy visualizes a loss of structural features. Sedimentation-velocity AUC confirms the changes of AdV quaternary structure upon heat-treatment with formation of high molecular weight species (HMWS). Density gradient equilibrium AUC shows the formation of lower density species and fluorescence detection during SV-AUC with SYBR green further indicates the presence of cargo and capsid within these HMWS. During a storage stability study, the combination of nanoDSF/DLS, DSF and SV-AUC provided a beneficial methods set to assess changes in AdVs with optimized sample consumption.

articles.title: Nitrosating agent scavengers: Structural characterization and ICH M7 safety assessment of byproducts formed under forced nitrosation conditions.
articles.abstract: N-Nitrosamines are considered to be "cohort of concern" chemicals under ICH M7 guidelines, due to the high carcinogenic potency observed in rodent bioassays for some structures within the class. Because of this, these compounds are often assigned very low control limits, on the order of ng/day. The formation of complex nitrosamines (such as N-nitrosamine drug substance related impurities or NDSRIs) may be suppressed by the addition of small molecule inhibitors to drug product formulations. Such inhibitors have been reported in literature to prevent N-nitrosamine formation by reacting with nitrite or other adventitious nitrosating agents which might be present in drug products via redox reactions, nitration, diazotization of primary amines, and other pathways. However, there is limited information on the structures of the byproducts of these reactions. This poses a risk of the inhibitors themselves forming other potential mutagenic impurities which should be assessed. We exposed several inhibitors to pharmaceutically-relevant forced nitrosation conditions and characterized the resulting byproducts. None of the inhibitors evaluated in this work formed a reasonably-expected nitrosamine or nitrosating agent. Two of the byproducts were classified as ICH M7 Class 3 impurities, based on structural analysis with in silico tools. However, the potential risk posed by these impurities is considered acceptable, in accordance with ICH M7 principles, based on human exposure through metabolism and/or diet. No mutagenicity risk was identified for all other byproducts. Therefore, their use as inhibitors of nitrosamine formation in drug products carries no additional carcinogenic risk beyond that of their current applications in the pharmaceutical industry.

articles.title: Atomic layer deposition of antigen-decorated phage-like particles as a platform for thermally stable, single-injection antiviral vaccines.
articles.abstract: Overcoming barriers to the distribution, availability, and effectiveness of vaccines, are major public health challenges. For example, thermal instabilities of vaccines result in the need for strict cold-chain conditions during storage and shipping. In addition, many vaccines require the administration of multiple vaccine doses per individual for protective and durable immunity. In this study, we describe the combination of a SARS-CoV-2 receptor binding domain (RBD) lambda phage-like particle (PLP) vaccine platform with our spray-drying and atomic layer deposition (ALD) formulation to generate highly thermostable single-dose immunogens. We show that ALD formulated SARS-CoV-2 RBD PLP vaccines retain potent immunogenicity in mice following incubation for one month at temperatures up to 50°C. In addition, mice immunized with a single dose of ALD formulated SARS-CoV-2 RBD PLP vaccines developed SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibody responses similar to those induced by standard prime-boost regimens and were strongly protected against SARS-CoV-2 infection and disease. These data suggest that ALD-coated PLP-based vaccine formulations can address two critical barriers to effective deployment of antiviral vaccines-thermal stability and single-shot dosing.

articles.title: Model-based interspecies scaling of LPS-induced inflammation.
articles.abstract: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) challenge studies in animal models and healthy volunteers are widely used to investigate inflammatory cytokine responses and evaluate anti-inflammatory therapies. Quantitative interspecies differences complicate translation of anti-inflammatory responses and their pharmacological modulation from animals to humans. This study aimed to demonstrate how a model-based framework can be used to characterize LPS-induced cytokine responses and quantify interspecies differences towards improving animal-to-human translation. To this end, we utilized data from published LPS challenge studies in humans, pigs, and rats, from which study characteristics, LPS doses, and concentration-time profiles of interleukin-6 (IL-6) and tumour necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) were extracted. For each species, cytokine dynamics were characterized using a kinetic-pharmacodynamic (K-PD) model with a turnover model structure where LPS stimulated cytokine production. Delay differential equations (DDEs) were used to account for delayed cytokine production. The model framework adequately described species-specific IL-6 and TNF-α responses and enabled quantitative comparison of LPS effects on cytokine production. Overall, this study demonstrates how LPS challenge data can be integrated into a quantitative framework for investigating interspecies differences. The framework provides a foundation for quantitative translation of inflammatory responses from animal models to humans.

articles.title: Macelignan attenuates LPS-induced hippocampal memory impairment by suppressing HMGB1/TLR4/NLRP3-mediated microglial pyroptosis.
articles.abstract: Neuroinflammation is a pivotal pathological process in neurological disorders. Microglial pyroptosis, a lytic and inflammatory form of programmed cell death, critically exacerbates neuroinflammation and causes neuronal damage. Macelignan has neuroprotective properties, but its mechanism in regulating microglial pyroptosis remains unclear. This study investigated whether macelignan protects against neuroinflammation by inhibiting microglial pyroptosis via high mobility group box 1 (HMGB1). In vitro, lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated BV2 microglial cells were treated with macelignan alone or combined with glycyrrhizin (an HMGB1 inhibitor) or disulfiram (a pyroptosis inhibitor). Macelignan suppressed M1 polarization and inflammatory cytokine release, as assessed by CCK-8, ELISA, and morphological analysis. Molecular docking predicted a potential interaction between macelignan and HMGB1. Western blot and immunofluorescence showed that macelignan downregulated HMGB1/TLR4/NLRP3 signaling, inhibited NLRP3 inflammasome activation, caspase-1 cleavage, and GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis, phenocopying glycyrrhizin. In a microglia-neuron co-culture model, conditioned medium from macelignan-treated BV2 cells reduced apoptosis in hippocampal HT22 neurons. In vivo, LPS-injected C57BL/6 mice were treated with low- or high-dose macelignan or glycyrrhizin (positive control). Macelignan attenuated hippocampal pyroptosis and neuronal damage, and behavioral tests revealed improved hippocampal-dependent memory. Collectively, these findings suggest that macelignan alleviates neuroinflammation and cognitive impairment likely by suppressing the HMGB1/NLRP3 axis to inhibit microglial pyroptosis, offering a potential mechanism for its neuroprotective action.

articles.title: PDE4B Inhibition Attenuates Intestinal Inflammation with Reducing Glycolysis in Macrophages.
articles.abstract: Accumulating evidence underscores that PDE4B expression is significantly upregulated in patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). However, its therapeutic potential and the underlying molecular mechanisms in pediatric IBD remain poorly defined. In this study, multiple public datasets were analyzed to characterize PDE4B expression in pediatric IBD. This was followed by therapeutic evaluation in mice colitis models to validate the efficacy of PDE4B inhibition in vivo. Analysis of public datasets revealed a marked elevation of PDE4B in pediatric IBD cohorts. Mechanistically, we demonstrated that a PDE4B inhibitor effectively suppressed LPS-induced inflammatory responses in primary blood samples from pediatric patients. In murine models, pharmacological inhibition of PDE4B significantly attenuated intestinal inflammation in both DSS- and LPS-induced colitis models. Furthermore, treatment with the PDE4B inhibitor successfully alleviated established chronic mucosal injury and preserved goblet cell integrity in spontaneous Il10-/- mice. Furthermore, 16S rRNA gene sequencing demonstrated that PDE4B inhibition was associated with a partial restoration of gut microbiota diversity and a reduction in specific bacterial dysbiosis. At the molecular level, the inhibitor promoted the activation of the anti-inflammatory mediator p-CREB while concurrently abrogating pro-inflammatory p-STAT3 signaling. Notably, the suppression of pathological glycolysis by the inhibitor was closely accompanied by the metabolic reprogramming and enhanced anti-inflammatory function. In conclusion, these findings suggest that targeting PDE4B represents a potential therapeutic approach for pediatric IBD by modulating macrophage immunometabolism and restoring intestinal homeostasis.

articles.title: A selective GLT-1 positive allosteric modulator produces antinociception in a mouse model of neuropathic pain.
articles.abstract: Neuropathic pain is a chronic somatosensory disorder that remains difficult to treat due to limited efficacy and adverse effects of current therapies. Modulation of the astrocytic glutamate transporter GLT-1 (EAAT2), a key regulator of extracellular glutamate homeostasis, represents a promising non-opioid strategy. While GLT-1 expression enhancers reduce nociception in preclinical models, the development of selective pharmacological modulators remains challenging. Here, we evaluated the antinociceptive efficacy and pharmacological profile of NA-014, a novel positive allosteric modulator (PAM) of GLT-1, in a mouse model of neuropathic pain. Using the spared nerve injury model of neuropathic pain in adult male and female C57BL/6J mice, we assessed evoked and non-evoked pain behaviors, including mechanical allodynia (von Frey), cold hypersensitivity (acetone test), conditioned place preference, and mechanical conflict avoidance. NA-014 reduced mechanical allodynia and cold hypersensitivity in both sexes, without producing detectable locomotor or cognitive impairment or anxiety-like behavior at effective doses. Both systemic and intrathecal delivery produced robust antinociceptive effects, whereas administration into the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) was ineffective. Intrathecal, but not ACC, GLT-1 knockdown attenuated the antinociceptive effects of NA-014, consistent with a contribution from GLT-1 within the intrathecal/spinal compartment under the experimental conditions. These findings demonstrate that NA-014 produces robust antinociceptive effects in a preclinical model of neuropathic pain and support a contribution of GLT-1 within the intrathecal/spinal compartment to its activity. These findings support GLT-1 PAMs as promising non-opioid pharmacological candidates for the treatment of neuropathic pain.

articles.title: Catalpol Prevents Ovariectomy-Induced Bone Loss Through DUSP6-Mediated Suppression of SMAD2/NFATc1 Signaling and Osteoclast Differentiation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Postmenopausal osteoporosis is characterized by estrogen deficiency-induced disruption of bone remodeling. Catalpol exerts bone-protective effects, but its direct molecular target and underlying mechanism remain incompletely understood. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether catalpol attenuates ovariectomy (OVX)-induced bone loss through dual-specificity phosphatase 6 (DUSP6)/SMAD family member 2 (SMAD2)/nuclear factor of activated T cells cytoplasmic 1 (NFATc1) signaling and to evaluate its effects on osteogenic differentiation. METHODS: OVX rats were treated with catalpol (5, 10, or 20 mg/kg) or alendronate for 12 weeks. Bone microarchitecture, bone remodeling, and osteoclast-related changes were assessed. In RAW264.7 cells, DUSP6 dependence was examined by knockdown and rescue experiments. Catalpol-DUSP6 interaction was evaluated by molecular docking, cellular thermal shift assay, and microscale thermophoresis (MST). Osteogenic differentiation was assessed in MC3T3-E1 cells. RESULTS: Catalpol improved trabecular microarchitecture, increased osteoblast-related histomorphometric parameters, and suppressed osteoclast formation in OVX rats. Catalpol increased DUSP6 expression and DUSP6-SMAD2 association, reduced SMAD2 phosphorylation, and inhibited NFATc1 nuclear accumulation. DUSP6 knockdown attenuated these effects, whereas DUSP6 restoration restored catalpol responsiveness. MST demonstrated direct catalpol binding to WT-DUSP6 (Kd = 3.617 μM), while mutation of predicted binding residues weakened the interaction (Kd = 48.12 μM). Catalpol also enhanced alkaline phosphatase-positive area, matrix mineralization, and osteogenic protein expression. CONCLUSION: Catalpol attenuates OVX-induced bone loss through DUSP6-mediated suppression of SMAD2/NFATc1-dependent osteoclastogenesis and additionally promotes osteogenic differentiation in vitro.

articles.title: Immunomodulatory Effects of Dodelate C against Plasmodium by Reshaping Macrophage Function.
articles.abstract: This study investigated the effect and molecular mechanism of Dodelate C, a sesquiterpenoid isolated from Dobinea delavayi, in regulating macrophage function during malaria. Its antiplasmodial activity was tested in vitro against Plasmodium falciparum 3D7, and macrophage regulatory effects examined in vivo in Plasmodium yoelii-infected mice. Cytokine levels were quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA); macrophage polarization was analyzed via flow cytometry, with proliferation and phagocytosis measured by Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) and neutral red uptake assays. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and dynamics simulations identified potential targets, with key protein expression validated by Western blot. Dodelate C exerted robust antiplasmodial activity both in vitro and in vivo. In infected mice, it significantly reduced serum interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) and nitric oxide (NO) levels, increased total macrophages, and markedly decreased the M1/M2 ratio. At non-cytotoxic concentrations in RAW 264.7 cells, Dodelate C enhanced macrophage phagocytic function and regulated macrophage polarization: it downregulated CD86 and pro-inflammatory factors (NO, tumor necrosis factor-alpha [TNF-α], and interleukin-1 beta [IL-1β]) to suppress the M1 phenotype, while upregulating CD206 and interleukin-10 (IL-10) to promote M2. Additionally, Dodelate C elevated Beclin-1 and the microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 (LC3)-II/LC3-I ratio, modulating peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) and phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/Akt) signaling by upregulating PPARγ/retinoid X receptor alpha (RXRα) and reducing insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor (IGF1R)/Akt/mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) phosphorylation. These findings show Dodelate C modulates macrophage function by balancing polarization and regulating autophagy, driving its antimalarial efficacy.

articles.title: Insulin plays a key role in dysregulation of energy homeostasis in tumor-bearing mice that is ameliorated by olanzapine and diazoxide.
articles.abstract: While cancer patients often show metabolic disturbances, the underlying mechanisms are not well understood. The present study examined changes in plasma glucose and food intake in tumor-bearing (TB) mice and the possible therapeutic effects of the antipsychotic drug olanzapine and the insulin secretion inhibitor diazoxide on these changes. TB mice were established by transplantation with mouse osteosarcoma AXT cells. Food intake and plasma glucose, but not body weight, were decreased whereas plasma insulin was increased in TB mice. Hypothalamic mRNAs of neuropeptide Y (NPY) and agouti-related peptide (AgRP), known as feeding-promoting peptides, were increased in TB mice. Among cytokines investigated, hypothalamic keratinocyte-derived cytokine (KC) was increased in TB mice, but KC injection did not affect food intake. In the glucose tolerance test there was no difference between control and TB mice. In contrast, in TB mice hyperglycemia in the pyruvate tolerance test was decreased and hepatic glycogen and mRNAs of rate-limiting enzymes in gluconeogenesis were decreased. Moreover, in TB mice acute injection of either olanzapine or diazoxide increased plasma glucose but not food intake. Repeated injection of these drugs to TB mice not only increased plasma glucose but also decreased tumor weight. These results show that anorexia and hypoglycemia occur in TB mice without alteration in body weight. It is also suggested that in TB mice anorexia cannot be explained by changes in hypothalamic NPY/AgRP and KC and that hypoglycemia occurs due to decreased hepatic glucose production, possibly by hyperinsulinemia. Moreover, both olanzapine and diazoxide ameliorate hypoglycemia in TB mice.

articles.title: Isoalantolactone suppresses non-small cell lung cancer progression by inducing ferroptosis through HSC70-mediated GPX4 degradation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Isoalantolactone (IAL), a sesquiterpene lactone derived from Inula helenium L. and Inula racemosa Hook. f., exhibits anti-inflammatory and anticancer properties. This study investigated the effects of IAL against non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). METHODS: The anticancer activity and potential mechanisms of IAL were evaluated in A549 and H1299 cells using CCK-8 proliferation assays, colony formation assays, flow cytometry, and RNA sequencing. The molecular target of IAL was identified through Drug Affinity Responsive Target Stability (DARTS) coupled with mass spectrometry. The binding between IAL and its target, HSC70, was validated by molecular docking and surface plasmon resonance (SPR). The functional role of HSC70 was confirmed via co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) and lentiviral-mediated short hairpin RNA (shRNA) knockdown. In vivo efficacy was evaluated in subcutaneous xenograft models, with IAL administered every other day. RESULTS: IAL directly bound to HSC70 with a dissociation constant (Kd) of 1.07 μM and promoted glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) degradation. IAL induced hallmark features of ferroptosis, including lipid peroxidation, iron accumulation, glutathione (GSH) depletion, and oxidized glutathione (GSSG) elevation. In vitro, HSC70 knockdown abrogated IAL-induced GPX4 degradation and ferroptosis. In subcutaneous xenograft models, IAL significantly suppressed tumor growth without evident toxicity and was accompanied by HSC70/GPX4 changes consistent with the in vitro mechanism. CONCLUSIONS: IAL directly targets HSC70 and promotes GPX4 degradation, inducing ferroptosis in NSCLC cells. In subcutaneous xenograft models, IAL suppresses tumor growth with HSC70/GPX4 changes consistent with this mechanism and no overt toxicity at the tested doses. These findings support further preclinical evaluation of IAL.

articles.title: Podophyllotoxin-induced mammary gland injury via the gut-mammary gland axis mediated by gut microbiota-derived metabolite PAG and aberrant EGFR signaling in SD rats based on the toxicological evidence chain (TEC) concept.
articles.abstract: Podophyllotoxin is a lignan isolated from Dysosma versipellis with well-established antitumor activity. In this study, we applied an upgraded toxicological evidence chain 2.0 framework to characterize podophyllotoxin-induced mammary toxicity in female rats and to probe the distal regulatory mechanism operating through the gut-mammary axis. Repeated oral exposure provoked acute toxic signs in the animals, and histomorphometric analysis revealed a significant loss of collagen fibers in mammary tissue. 16S rRNA sequencing showed reduced gut microbial diversity, marked expansion of the opportunistic pathogen Escherichia_710834, and concurrent depletion of short-chain fatty acid producers such as Ligilactobacillus. Raman spectroscopy combined with targeted metabolomics uncovered 53 differentially abundant metabolites. Among these, four microbial-derived compounds-p-cresol, phenylacetylglycine, skatole, and trimethylamine N-oxide-correlated positively with Escherichia_710834 abundance. Further screening prioritized phenylacetylglycine and the epidermal growth factor receptor as the most credible ligand-receptor pair. Microscale thermophoresis confirmed a strong direct interaction, and qPCR revealed upregulated expression of downstream genes linked to proliferation and inflammation. Together, our findings define a complete causal pathway: podophyllotoxin perturbs the gut microbiome, driving excess production of phenylacetylglycine, which enters the circulation, engages mammary epidermal growth factor receptor, and aberrantly activates transcriptional responses that ultimately culminate in mammary tissue damage.

articles.title: Age-conditioned nanomedicine for Parkinson's disease: Pharmaceutical design, brain exposure and regenerative repair.
articles.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is predominantly a disorder of older adults, yet nanomedicine studies often optimize carrier performance in young models and use blood-brain barrier (BBB) crossing as the principal success criterion. This mini-review reframes PD nanomedicine as an age-conditioned pharmaceutical design problem in which formulation attributes, route of administration, biological identity, regional exposure, active-payload release, and clearance are jointly determined by the host. Age-related neurovascular remodeling, altered endothelial transport, microglial priming, reduced interstitial and glymphatic clearance, and changes in protein-corona formation are evaluated as variables that can modify both efficacy and safety. Lipid and polymer nanoparticles, drug nanocrystals, intranasal systems, alginate and chitosan formulations, hydrogels, biomimetic carriers, catalytic nanozymes, graphene, and carbon-nanotube interfaces are compared according to the formulation bottleneck they address. Particular attention is given to dopamine stabilization, alpha-synuclein inhibitors and gene-silencing cargo, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory nanozymes, and biomaterial-assisted dopaminergic regeneration. Across platforms, the key pharmaceutical requirement is to connect a critical material attribute to intact-carrier exposure, release of active drug at the relevant site, proximal target engagement, and route-specific safety. A concise translational framework is proposed that combines age-relevant models with critical quality attributes, washout and clearance studies, repeated-dose safety, and manufacturability. Treating aging as a design variable rather than a demographic descriptor should improve the relevance of preclinical formulation development for PD.

articles.title: 3D bioprinting of alginate-gelatin inks with lipid nanoparticles for localized drug delivery in glioblastoma therapy.
articles.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) management is severely limited by systemic barriers, including poor blood-brain barrier penetration and off-target toxicities. Localized delivery platforms offer a promising alternative by providing prolonged therapeutic concentrations directly at the tumor site post-resection. In this study, 3D-printed scaffolds composed of sodium alginate (SA) and gelatin (GEL) inks loaded with lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) were developed as a platform for local delivery of nucleic acid molecules (siRNA fluorescent). To optimize printability and structural stability, 2 % SA (w/v) and 10 % GEL (w/v) solutions in PBS buffer (pH 7.4) were mixed at different volume ratios, including 1:1, 2:1, 5:1, and 1:5. The 2:1 SA:GEL ratio produced the most stable and well-defined printed structures. Three LNPs incorporation strategies were also evaluated, and pre-incorporation of LNPs into the SA solution resulted in the most homogeneous and stable scaffolds. Rheological analysis confirmed the ink's suitability for extrusion-based bioprinting, demonstrating pseudoplastic, shear-thinning behavior and a 55 % recovery rate essential for structural integrity. Printed scaffolds were fabricated at 13 % and 35 % infill densities and characterized by morphology, rheological behavior, release profiles, and uptake in U87 human glioblastoma cells. In vitro siRNA-LNPs release from the selected ink was architecture-dependent, reaching completion within 24 h at 35 % infill and within 8 h at 13 % infill. Furthermore, the scaffold-integrated LNPs system enabled efficient delivery of fluorescently labelled siRNA to U87 cell. These findings validate the potential of SA-GEL scaffolds as biocompatible platforms for the controlled administration of siRNA-loaded LNPs.

articles.title: MasR agonist AVE0991 ameliorates EAE: potential involvement of the Nrf2-dependent TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 pathway.
articles.abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic inflammatory demyelinating disease of the central nervous system (CNS). Mas receptor (MasR) constitutes the counter-regulatory arm of the renin-angiotensin system. Despite well-established anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective effects of MasR, its functional roles and regulatory mechanisms in MS remain elusive. Herein, we established an experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) model in female C57BL/6 mice by immunization with MOG35-55, and prophylactically treated the mice with the selective MasR agonist AVE0991 starting on day 8 post-immunization for 14 consecutive days. The results showed that AVE0991 treatment reversed the downregulated MasR expression in the spinal cord of EAE mice, effectively alleviated neurological functional impairments, and mitigated excessive inflammatory infiltration in the CNS. MasR was verified to be expressed in IBA1+ cells, and transcriptomic profiling indicated its close association with immune regulation. In lipopolysaccharide-stimulated BV2 cells, AVE0991 significantly inhibited inflammatory responses. Mechanistically, MasR activation by AVE0991 facilitated Nrf2 nuclear translocation, thereby suppressing the TLR4/MyD88 signaling cascade and NF-κB nuclear translocation, and eventually inhibiting NLRP3. Consistently, the anti-inflammatory effects of AVE0991 were fully abolished by the MasR inhibitor A779, TLR4 agonist Neoseptin 3 or Nrf2 inhibitor ML385. And the protein-level alterations of the above molecules were also recapitulated in spinal cord homogenates from EAE mice. Collectively, our data suggest that AVE0991-mediated MasR activation ameliorates neurological deficits and neuroinflammation in EAE, possibly via Nrf2-dependent regulation of the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 cascade. These findings identify a MasR-associated regulatory axis linked to neuroinflammation, which may provide a potential therapeutic strategy for MS.

articles.title: Temporal effects of acute kidney injury on hepatic function, drug elimination, and transcriptomics in a mouse ischemic reperfusion injury model.
articles.abstract: While the effect of acute kidney injury on the kidney and the elimination of renally cleared drugs is well understood, the impact on liver clearance is less characterized. Therefore, using the mouse kidney ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) acute kidney injury model, we examined the pharmacokinetics (PK) of 2 hepatically cleared drugs, pitavastatin and antipyrine, pre-IRI and post-IRI, as well as changes in gene expression in liver and kidney, and the impact on kidney and liver injury markers. Post-IRI, the glomerular filtration rate was reduced by 99% at 2 hours and improved mildly by 72 hours (82% reduction in glomerular filtration rate). Additionally, post-IRI, kidney and liver damage biomarkers increased, as well as the uremic toxin, indoxyl sulfate, all of which were restored partially on day 16 post-IRI. The terminal exposure of pitavastatin and antipyrine was increased when dosed 2 and 24 hours post-IRI, compared with when dosed to control mice. The change in pitavastatin exposure could be explained by decreased clearance, but for antipyrine, the effect was complex and likely multifactorial. Altered expression of drug metabolizing enzymes and transporter genes in the liver was observed post-IRI. In addition, increased mRNA expression of genes involved in various pathways such as tryptophan metabolism were observed from day 1 to 16 post-IRI. Changes in the kynurenine pathway possibly contributed to changes in drug elimination because of changes in energy status. Overall, this study supports renohepatic crosstalk post-IRI that impacts hepatic clearance mechanisms. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: The elimination of the hepatically cleared drugs, pitavastatin and antipyrine, decreased rapidly after ischemic injury in a mouse ischemia-reperfusion acute kidney injury model, indicating crosstalk between the kidney and liver after acute kidney injury. Long-lasting changes in mRNA levels of transporters and enzymes were observed in hepatic tissues, but it is unlikely that these explained the acute decrease in elimination of test drugs. Changes in the kynurenine pathway, involved in energy generation, could possibly contribute to acute effects on hepatic drug elimination.

articles.title: Investigation of the pharmacokinetics, metabolism, and clearance pathways of a heterobifunctional BRM degrader delivered by a TROP2-targeting antibody.
articles.abstract: The BRM protein is an important therapeutic target for BRG1-deficient non-small-cell lung cancer. A potent VHL-based proteolysis-targeting chimera targeting BRM, A515, was discovered but exhibited rapid systemic clearance and no oral bioavailability in rats. To overcome these pharmacokinetic challenges, an antibody-drug conjugate was developed for tumor-targeted delivery of A515. To facilitate this approach, an A515 linker-drug was generated, and in vitro assays confirmed efficient payload release by cathepsin B and lysosomal enzymes. Conjugation of this linker-drug to a TROP2-targeting antibody resulted in an antibody-drug conjugate that demonstrated tumor growth inhibition in an HCC515 xenograft model as well as high tumor concentrations of A515. The metabolism and clearance pathways of the A515 payload were further investigated in a study with bile duct-cannulated rats, and urinary excretion, biliary excretion, and metabolism were determined to be significant clearance pathways for A515. Both in vitro and in vivo metabolite identification studies showed that oxidative N-dealkylation leading to cleavage within the heterobifunctional degrader was the major metabolic pathway for A515, and this biotransformation was found to be largely mediated by CYP3A enzymes. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This study investigated the metabolism and disposition pathways of a TROP2-BRM degrader antibody conjugate and its payload in vitro and in vivo. The results support (1) the utility of antibody conjugation in overcoming poor DMPK properties for delivering the payload drug to the site of action and (2) the critical role of ADC linker cleavage and payload release as well as the subsequent disposition of the payload in enabling the ADC approach.

articles.title: LIM kinase inhibitors attenuate prostate enlargement and bladder outlet obstruction-associated detrusor pressure in rat models relevant to mixed lower urinary tract symptoms.
articles.abstract: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and overactive bladder (OAB) frequently coexist in men, producing mixed lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) that are inadequately managed by current combination pharmacotherapies. LIM kinase (LIMK) regulates actin cytoskeletal remodeling and smooth muscle tone. Here, we evaluated the in vivo effects of 2 LIMK inhibitors, SR7826 and LIMKi3, on prostate and bladder function in rat models of BPH and bladder outlet obstruction (BOO). In BPH rats, the prostate index was reduced by 0.080 ± 0.018 (SR7826, P < .01) and 0.058 ± 0.018 (LIMKi3, P < .05). Epithelial thickness was reduced by 17.71 ± 2.25 μm and 18.27 ± 1.72 μm, respectively (both P < .001). In the prostate, desmin decreased with both inhibitors (P < .05), α-smooth muscle actin decreased with LIMKi3 (P < .001), and vimentin increased with LIMKi3 (P < .01). LIMKi3, but not SR7826, reduced bladder index by 0.009 ± 0.002 (P < .05). Bladder wall structure and cholinergic-induced contractility were preserved. In BOO rats, maximum detrusor pressure was reduced by 32.2 ± 5.4 cm H2O (SR7826) and 32.8 ± 4.3 cm H2O (LIMKi3) (both P < .001). In conclusion, LIMK inhibition suppressed prostatic hyperplasia and altered prostatic contraction-associated protein expression in BPH rats, and reduced BOO-associated maximum detrusor pressure without impairing baseline cholinergic contractility. LIMK1/2 inhibition may represent a novel, pathophysiology-driven therapeutic strategy for the prostatic and bladder components of mixed LUTS. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Current pharmacotherapy for mixed lower urinary tract symptoms relies on combining α1-adrenoceptor antagonists (α1-blockers) and antimuscarinics-drugs with distinct targets and compounding adverse effects. This study demonstrates that LIM kinase inhibitors reduce prostatic hyperplasia and bladder outlet obstruction-associated maximum detrusor pressure in rat models while preserving baseline cholinergic bladder contractility, identifying LIM kinase as a candidate cross-organ target relevant to both voiding and storage dysfunction.

articles.title: Silylated withaferin A analogues display multi-stage HIV-1 inhibition with optimized in vitro potency and favorable predicted ADME properties.
articles.abstract: Despite advances in antiretroviral therapy, toxicity problems, emergence of drug-resistant HIV-1 (human immunodeficiency virus 1) strains and viral reservoirs, emphasize the urgent need for new anti-HIV drugs. Withaferin A, a natural steroidal lactone first isolated from the medicinal plant Withania somnifera (L.) Dunal (Ashwagandha), has emerged as a promising lead scaffold with proven pharmacological properties. Based on previous studies highlighting the therapeutic potential of withaferin A and the emerging role of organosilicon motifs in drug design, we explored and enlarged the chemical space of this steroidal framework as a basis to broaden the current antiretroviral chemotherapy. The present study reports the synthesis of thirty withaferin A-silyl ether analogues, including two twin compounds and three silyl-ester analogues reported for the first time. The antiretroviral activity of this compound series was evaluated, and five inhibitors were selected for mechanistic studies to define their mechanism of action in the HIV-1 replication cycle. Withaferin A and the selected analogues primarily acts through viral integration and post-transcriptional stages. Notably, some analogues redirect the withaferin A main mechanism, also affecting HIV envelope and reverse transcription. This multi-step behaviour may provide an advantage to overcome the drawbacks of the current therapy. In addition, structure-activity relationships and in silico ADME studies were employed to understand the structural requirements and pharmacokinetic properties of this series of analogues. The results herein underscore withaferin A as a versatile structural platform to develop new antiretroviral drugs.

articles.title: Perioperative pulmonary aspiration reports associated with GLP-1 receptor agonists: a pharmacovigilance analysis of FAERS.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide - 1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are increasingly prescribed for the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity. Although these agents provide substantial metabolic and cardiovascular benefits, they also delay gastric emptying, which may increase the risk of perioperative pulmonary aspiration during anesthesia. Real-world evidence evaluating this potential safety concern remains limited. We conducted a retrospective pharmacovigilance study using reports from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) from January 2016 through March 2024. A perioperative-enriched cohort was identified by restricting reports to those listing general anesthetic or neuromuscular blocking agents as surrogate markers of a perioperative setting. Patients were classified into three mutually exclusive groups: GLP-1 receptor agonists, sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT-2) inhibitors as an active comparator, and a background surgical population. Pulmonary aspiration events were identified using MedDRA preferred terms. Disproportionality analyses were performed using reporting odds ratios (RORs), and Firth penalized multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate independent predictors of aspiration after adjustment for age, sex, and concomitant opioid use, because exposed events were sparse. After deduplication, a total of 41,308 unique perioperative reports were identified, including 158 reports involving GLP-1 receptor agonists and 174 involving SGLT-2 inhibitors. Pulmonary aspiration showed non-significantly higher reporting odds among GLP-1 RA users (ROR 1.27, P = 0.56). In the Firth penalized adjusted analysis, GLP-1 RA exposure was associated with numerically higher, but statistically non-significant, adjusted reporting odds of pulmonary aspiration (aOR 2.08; P = 0.185). SGLT-2 inhibitor exposure showed numerically lower but statistically non-significant reporting odds of pulmonary aspiration than the background cohort (aOR 0.27; P = 0.059); this estimate rests on a single event and should not be interpreted as a protective effect. Concomitant opioid use was independently associated with aspiration (aOR 2.12; P < 0.001). In this perioperative-enriched FAERS analysis, neither the unadjusted disproportionality analysis nor the adjusted model demonstrated a statistically significant association between GLP-1 receptor agonist exposure and pulmonary aspiration, although a non-significant numerical trend was observed. Given the small number of events and the inherent limitations of spontaneous reporting data, these findings are hypothesis-generating, require prospective validation, and should not on their own guide individual perioperative decision-making.

articles.title: Rutin plus vitamin C attenuate acute doxorubicin-induced liver toxicity in rats.
articles.abstract: Doxorubicin (DOX) is widely used to treat hepatocellular carcinoma, but its use is limited by dose-dependent hepatotoxicity associated with oxidative stress and inflammation. Protective adjunct therapies that reduce liver injury without compromising anticancer efficacy remain a clinical challenge. Here, we evaluated the hepatoprotective effects of combined rutin and vitamin C administration in a rat model of acute DOX-induced liver injury. Forty-eight male albino rats (170-180 g) were randomly assigned to six groups of eight animals each: group I (distilled water vehicle control, orally), group II (DOX alone, 15 mg/kg intraperitoneally on day 12), group III (metformin, 250 mg/kg orally, daily + DOX), group IV (VitC+DOX), group V (RUT+DOX), and group VI (RUT+VitC+DOX). All groups except the control received a single intraperitoneal injection of DOX (15 mg/kg) on day 12, after daily oral dosing from days 1 to 14. Animals were sacrificed on day 14 to capture the acute phase of DOX-induced hepatotoxicity, which is well documented to peak within 48-72 h after high single doses of anthracyclines. Biochemical assays, oxidative stress markers, pro-inflammatory mediators, and histopathological analyses showed that co-treatment significantly restored antioxidant enzyme activities, reduced lipid peroxidation and reactive oxygen/nitrogen species, and attenuated inflammatory responses compared with DOX alone. The combination was statistically superior to either agent alone across all primary endpoints, with biochemical improvements comparable in magnitude to those observed in the metformin reference group. Histological analysis confirmed that combination therapy preserved liver architecture. These results indicate that co-administration of rutin and vitamin C provides greater hepatoprotection than either agent alone and may serve as an adjunctive strategy to mitigate DOX-induced hepatotoxicity.

articles.title: In Vitro assessment of clarithromycin and erythromycin depletion in the presence of andrographolide using human liver microsomes.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Andrographolide is a major bioactive compound of Andrographis paniculata, a medicinal herb widely used in Asia. Previous in vitro studies have reported effects of andrographolide on CYP3A4 expression and activity. However, potential pharmacokinetic interactions with the macrolide antibiotics clarithromycin and erythromycin remain poorly characterized. This study investigated the effect of andrographolide on their in vitro depletion using pooled human liver microsomes (HLMs). METHODS: Clarithromycin and erythromycin (1 µM each) were incubated in pooled HLMs with or without andrographolide at 2, 10, or 20 μM, corresponding to approximately 10-, 50-, and 100-fold the reported peak concentration (Cmax), respectively. Parent-antibiotic depletion was monitored by LC-MS/MS, and depletion rates were estimated by linear regression. RESULTS: Andrographolide did not significantly alter clarithromycin depletion at two or 10 µM (p = 0.1906 and 0.7898), whereas a significant difference was observed at 20 µM (p = 0.0321). The estimated effects had wide 95% confidence intervals. Erythromycin depletion was significantly altered at all concentrations, with relative differences of 38.5% (95% CI, 28.5%-48.5%), 33.5% (28.6%-38.3%), and 66.2% (57.0%-75.5%) at 2, 10, and 20 μM, respectively (all p < 0.0001). CONCLUSION: Andrographolide exerts a strong, concentration-dependent effect on in vitro erythromycin depletion in HLMs, whereas its effect on clarithromycin depletion is minimal and observed only at supra-therapeutic concentrations (100-fold Cmax). Given that effective concentrations exceeded physiological Cmax levels, clinical relevance remains uncertain. Further investigation is needed to clarify underlying metabolic mechanisms and evaluate in vivo translation.

articles.title: Association of finerenone plus tripterygium glycosides with proteinuria reduction in patients with diabetic kidney disease: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: We aimed to investigate the association of combined finerenone and tripterygium glycosides (TG) therapy with proteinuria reduction in patients with diabetic kidney disease (DKD). METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients with DKD and an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 15 to <60 mL/min/1.73 m2 who received finerenone alone (n = 167) or finerenone plus TG (n = 36) during January, 2023-April 2026. Longitudinal urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) was evaluated using adjusted linear mixed-effects models. Multiple subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed to assess the robustness of the findings. Associations between treatment groups and adverse events, including hyperkalemia, elevated liver transaminases, and a ≥1.5-fold increase in serum creatinine, were also evaluated. RESULTS: Among the 203 patients, the mean age was 65.1 years, the median UACR was 872.6 [273.8, 1723.1] mg/g, and the median eGFR was 46.2 [36.4, 53.3] mL/min/1.73 m2. Relative to finerenone alone, combination therapy was associated with an additional UACR reduction of 14.7% per 6 months (95% confidence interval [CI], [5.6%, 22.8%]; P = 0.002), equivalent to 27.5% per year (95% CI, [11.1%, 40.9%]). Combination therapy was associated with a higher rate of achieving a ≥50% reduction in UACR than finerenone alone (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 2.02; 95% CI, 1.17-3.48; P = 0.011). During follow-up, serum potassium increased to a greater extent in the combination therapy group (P = 0.031), whereas longitudinal changes in serum creatinine and eGFR did not differ significantly between the groups (both P > 0.05). However, the incidences of hyperkalemia and liver and kidney-related adverse events were also comparable between the groups (all P > 0.05). CONCLUSION: In patients with DKD and an eGFR of 15 to <60 mL/min/1.73 m2, combination therapy with TG and finerenone was associated with a greater reduction in UACR than finerenone alone, without a significant increase in the risk of the assessed adverse events. Further evaluation in prospective randomized trials is warranted.

articles.title: Population pharmacokinetics of vancomycin in patients with liver dysfunction.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Vancomycin is widely used in the treatment of serious infections caused by multidrug-resistant Gram-positive pathogens. However, the pharmacokinetic characteristics of vancomycin in patients with liver dysfunction remain inadequately characterized. This study aimed to develop a population pharmacokinetic (PopPK) model of vancomycin in patients with liver dysfunction and identify significant factors affecting plasma concentrations to guide individual therapy. METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, clinical data were collected from patients with liver dysfunction. A nonlinear mixed effects model was employed to describe the influence of covariates on vancomycin pharmacokinetics and to obtain the final PopPK model. Goodness-of-fit plots, bootstrap analysis, and visual predictive checks were applied to assess the model stability and predictive performance. RESULTS: A total of 163 observable concentrations from 105 patients with liver dysfunction were included for PopPK modeling. A one-compartment model with first-order elimination best described the data, yielding a central volume of distribution (V) of 147.47 L and clearance (CL) of 4.40 L/h. Albumin (ALB) and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) were identified as significant covariates on V and CL in the final PopPK model, respectively. Model validation further demonstrated the excellent stability and predictive performance. CONCLUSION: The PopPK model incorporating ALB and eGFR can be used for model-informed precision dosing in this population, potentially improving target attainment of vancomycin and reducing the risk of nephrotoxicity.

articles.title: Real-world pharmacovigilance analysis of adverse events associated with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor antidepressants in children and adolescents.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Depressive disorders are common in children and adolescents, with major depression affecting 3.7% of youth and subclinical symptoms affecting over one-fifth. Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), including fluoxetine, sertraline, and fluvoxamine, are prescribed for moderate-to-severe pediatric depression. However, real-world safety signals for specific SSRIs remain incompletely characterized because evidence derives mainly from randomized controlled trials with restrictive inclusion criteria, observational studies affected by prescribing bias, and spontaneous reporting systems without reliable exposure denominators. METHODS: We extracted reports from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System through the second quarter of 2026 for depressed children and adolescents aged 6-18 years receiving fluoxetine, sertraline, or fluvoxamine. Disproportionality analyses used reporting odds ratio, proportional reporting ratio, Bayesian confidence propagation neural network, and multi-item gamma Poisson shrinker to detect signals at system organ class and preferred term levels. Weibull models assessed time to onset, and network toxicology approaches explored candidate targets and pathways underlying the shared rhabdomyolysis signal. RESULTS: A total of 2,614 reports were included: 1,260 for fluoxetine, 1,278 for sertraline, and 76 for fluvoxamine. Psychiatric and nervous system disorders were the most frequently reported system organ classes for all three drugs. Fluoxetine showed prominent signals for serotonin syndrome, neuroleptic malignant syndrome, rhabdomyolysis, blood creatine phosphokinase increase, and acute kidney injury; sertraline showed strong signals for serotonin syndrome, urinary retention, intentional self-injury, rhabdomyolysis, hepatocellular injury, and respiratory failure. Rhabdomyolysis was reported in 39 fluoxetine cases (ROR = 4.26, 95% CI: 2.81-6.45) and 26 sertraline cases (ROR = 2.69, 95% CI: 1.71-4.24). Time-to-onset analyses revealed an early-failure Weibull pattern for both drugs, with median onsets of 24 and 30 days, respectively. Network toxicology analysis identified shared candidate targets including CYP3A4, CYP2D6, SLC6A4, MAOA, DRD1, DRD2, NOS2, and KCNH2, with enrichment in serotonergic synapse, oxidative stress, and hypoxia response pathways. CONCLUSION: This study provides evidence to prioritize symptoms, organ systems, and high-risk monitoring windows in pediatric SSRI prescribing. It offers the first systematic report of SSRI-associated rhabdomyolysis in children and adolescents and translates real-world pharmacovigilance signals into guidance for baseline risk assessment, early monitoring, family education, and symptom-driven laboratory testing.

articles.title: A standardized Orthosiphon aristatus extract improves forced-swimming performance and modulates hematological and hepatic biochemical parameters in paclitaxel-treated mice.
articles.abstract: Cancer-related fatigue is a prevalent and debilitating condition among patients undergoing chemotherapy, markedly impairing quality of life and treatment adherence. This multifactorial syndrome arises from both the malignancy itself and treatment-related toxicities, particularly those associated with neurotoxic and cytotoxic agents such as paclitaxel. Despite its high prevalence, effective and well-tolerated interventions for chemotherapy-induced fatigue remain limited. The present study evaluated the effects of Lanctos 75™ (C5OSEW5050ESA), a standardized polymolecular extract derived from Orthosiphon aristatus (Blume) Miq., on chemotherapy-associated physical performance in paclitaxel-treated mice. Thirty adult male mice were allocated to five groups (n = 6 per group). Lanctos 75™ (200 or 400 mg/kg/day) or rosmarinic acid (30 mg/kg/day) was administered orally for 7 days before paclitaxel exposure (10 mg/kg/day for 5 days). Physical performance was assessed using a modified forced swimming test, together with clinical observations, body weight, food and water intake, hematological parameters, serum biochemistry, and qualitative histopathology. Lanctos 75™-treated mice showed improved forced-swimming performance compared with the paclitaxel-treated control group. Paclitaxel alone was associated with reduced body weight and WBC count and with alterations in serum globulin, glucose, AST, and ALT, whereas these parameters were less altered in the Lanctos 75™-treated groups. Rosmarinic acid also showed activity in selected measured outcomes. As the forced-swimming paradigm assesses only a component of physical performance under experimental stress, the observed improvement does not demonstrate reversal of the multidimensional clinical syndrome of cancer-related fatigue. However, the overall findings indicate that Lanctos 75™ was associated with improved forced-swimming performance and differences in selected hematological and biochemical parameters in paclitaxel-treated mice. These preclinical observations warrant confirmation in adequately powered studies using complementary fatigue-related behavioral measures and direct mechanistic assessments.

articles.title: Expert-referenced evaluation of large language models for primary suspect drug identification in the FAERS database.
