articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Accurate identification of primary suspect drugs in adverse event reports is a critical component of post-marketing pharmacovigilance and serves as a foundation for downstream signal detection activities. However, causal attribution in spontaneous reporting systems such as the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) is inherently challenging. Traditional expert-based assessments are resource-intensive and difficult to scale, highlighting the need for complementary, reproducible approaches. This study aimed to evaluate the performance of large language models (LLMs) in identifying primary suspect drugs in adverse event reports against an expert reference standard. METHODS: Fifty FAERS case reports were randomly selected for evaluation. Three clinical pharmacy experts established the reference standard by adjudicating the primary suspect drug(s) for each case. LLM-based evaluations were conducted using multiple prompting strategies and model configurations. The performance of LLMs, pharmacy student evaluators, and original FAERS primary suspect designations (ROLE_COD) was assessed by calculating hit rates against the expert reference standard. RESULTS: The original FAERS designations demonstrated limited accuracy against the expert reference standard, with a hit rate of 0.778. In contrast, LLM-based assessments achieved consistently high hit rates ranging from 0.867 to 0.920 across diverse prompting strategies and model configurations. Student evaluators achieved a comparable hit rate of 0.872; however, LLM-based evaluations exhibited greater internal consistency and markedly shorter response times. CONCLUSION: LLM-based evaluations demonstrated high accuracy against expert assessments and favorable efficiency relative to student evaluators. These findings highlight the potential utility of LLMs as scalable, readily accessible decision-support tools in pharmacovigilance workflows.

articles.title: Reliability-aware molecular screening for drug-induced liver injury in predictive toxicology under chemical scaffold shift.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Drug-induced liver injury (DILI) remains a challenging endpoint in predictive toxicology because molecular datasets are limited, chemical scaffolds shift across data sources, and probability scores do not necessarily indicate prediction reliability. This study aimed to develop a reliability-aware molecular screening framework for DILI prediction under chemical scaffold shift. METHODS: We developed CC-SCAC-AFP, which combines an AttentiveFP ranking backbone with coverage-constrained split conformal prediction and adaptive novelty-conditioned calibration. The framework was evaluated on the Therapeutics Data Commons DILI task using leakage-audited Murcko-scaffold partitions, five seeds for model comparison, and 20 four-way scaffold splits for reliability analysis. DILIst and DILIrank 2.0 were reserved for strict external evaluation. RESULTS: AttentiveFP achieved an internal mean AUROC of 0.862 (standard deviation [SD], 0.023). Across 20 reliability splits at α = 0.10, CC-SCAC-AFP achieved empirical coverage of 0.949 (SD, 0.050), compared with 0.937 (SD, 0.054) for global split conformal prediction. The corresponding mean prediction-set sizes were 1.604 and 1.521, respectively, indicating that the additional coverage was largely attributable to increased conservatism rather than improved efficiency at matched set size. On external tests, AUROC was 0.598 for both DILIst and DILIrank 2.0. Coverage was 0.891 and 0.801, respectively, below the nominal 0.90 target. The DILIrank 2.0 Brier score of 0.348 was worse than that of a constant predictor based on the observed prevalence (0.249). DISCUSSION: CC-SCAC-AFP provides a chemically indexed, set-valued reliability screening framework for early DILI molecular prioritization and makes the coverage-efficiency trade-off explicit. Two-label prediction sets identify compounds requiring further review. Because source-domain calibration did not preserve the nominal coverage target on the external datasets, recalibration in the target domain is necessary before applying the framework to a new chemical library.

articles.title: 8,9-EET analogs protect glomerular cells from doxorubicin-induced toxicity.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Doxorubicin (DOX) is an anthracycline chemotherapeutic whose clinical utility is limited by dose-dependent nephrotoxicity that contributes to acute and chronic kidney injury. Podocytes are essential components of the glomerular filtration barrier and are particularly vulnerable to DOX-induced oxidative stress, cytoskeletal disruption, loss of adhesion, and apoptosis. Therapeutic strategies that protect podocytes without compromising anticancer efficacy therefore represent an important unmet need. This study investigated the protective mechanisms and translational potential of 8,9-epoxyeicosatrienoic acid (8,9-EET) analogs against DOX-induced podocyte injury. METHODS: Nineteen 8,9-EET analogs were screened in cultured podocytes exposed to DOX. Protective effects were evaluated by assessing cell viability, caspase-3/7 activation, reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, and focal adhesion integrity using confocal immunofluorescence analysis of vinculin. Selected analogs were also evaluated in DU145 prostate cancer and HCC1806 breast cancer cells to determine whether podocyte protection altered the anticancer activity of DOX. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: Several 8,9-EET analogs significantly improved podocyte viability and attenuated DOX-induced apoptosis, as demonstrated by reduced caspase-3/7 activation. DOX markedly disrupted focal adhesion complexes, decreasing vinculin number and area, whereas co-treatment with selected analogs preserved vinculin-associated focal adhesion integrity. Effective analogs also significantly reduced DOX-induced ROS generation, consistent with attenuation of oxidative stress. Importantly, selected analogs protected podocytes without compromising DOX anticancer activity in either DU145 or HCC1806 cells, supporting separation of renoprotective effects from the desired cytotoxic action of DOX. These findings identify selected 8,9-EET analogs as promising podocyte-protective agents against DOX-induced injury. Their protective effects were associated with reduced oxidative stress and apoptosis and preservation of focal adhesion architecture, suggesting coordinated maintenance of podocyte structural integrity and survival. Preservation of DOX anticancer activity in prostate and breast cancer cells further supports the translational potential of these compounds as adjunctive therapies during anthracycline chemotherapy. Collectively, targeting epoxy lipid signaling with 8,9-EET analogs may provide a strategy to limit chemotherapy-associated podocyte injury and preserve renal function without diminishing antitumor efficacy. These results support preclinical evaluation of lead analogs, including their pharmacological properties, renal protective efficacy, and therapeutic compatibility with DOX in relevant models. These findings warrant defining efficacy, safety, dosing, and translational feasibility in vivo.

articles.title: Cardamine flexuosa extract attenuates neutrophilic airway inflammation in a CSE/LPS-induced murine model.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a leading cause of disease- related mortality worldwide and is characterized by progressive airflow limitation accompanied by persistent neutrophilic airway inflammation. Macrophage activation plays a key role in this process through the production of pro- inflammatory mediators and neutrophil-attracting chemokines. METHODS: This study investigated the anti-inflammatory effects of Cardamine flexuosa extract (CFE) in macrophage and cigarette smoke extract (CSE)/lipopolysaccharide (LPS)- induced models, with emphasis on macrophage inflammatory responses and neutrophilic airway inflammation. RESULTS: In LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophages, CFE reduced nitric oxide production by 77.8% and decreased the secretion of TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, and matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), accompanied by reduced MAPK phosphorylation. In a murine model induced by intranasal administration of CSE and LPS, oral CFE reduced total inflammatory cell and neutrophil counts in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) by 53.9% and 82.9%, respectively, at 200 mg/kg compared with the CSE/LPS group. These effects were associated with reduced pulmonary expression of CXCL-1 and MIP-2 and decreased MAPK phosphorylation. Histological analysis demonstrated attenuation of inflammatory cell infiltration and mucus hypersecretion. CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate that CFE attenuates macrophage inflammatory responses and neutrophilic airway inflammation in the CSE/LPS-induced murine model, accompanied by reduced inflammatory mediator production and MAPK activation.

articles.title: Associated factors and dynamic coagulation changes of cefoperazone/sulbactam-associated coagulopathy: a retrospective case-control study from a single-center real-world ADR database.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Cefoperazone/sulbactam is associated with severe coagulopathy, believed to be mediated by its N-methylthiotetrazole side chain through inhibition of the vitamin K cycle; however, comprehensive real-world data on risk factors remain limited. This study aimed to identify potential factors associated with cefoperazone/sulbactam-induced coagulopathy and to characterize the dynamic changes in coagulation parameters in affected patients. METHODS: This retrospective case-control study identified 228 patients with adverse drug reactions (ADRs) from a hospital database. Patients were divided into a coagulopathy group (n = 25) and an other-ADR control group (n = 203); baseline characteristics and coagulation parameters (PT, INR, APTT, PLT) were compared. Firth penalized logistic regression was used in an exploratory analysis to identify factors independently associated with coagulopathy. RESULTS: Among the 228 patients with ADRs, 25 (11.0%) developed coagulopathy. Compared with the control group, the case group was significantly older (70.08 vs. 61.92 years, P = 0.020) and had higher proportions of renal disease (52.0% vs. 11.3%), heart failure (24.0% vs. 5.9%), diabetes (36.0% vs. 14.8%), and diuretic (80.0%) or anticoagulant (56.0%) use (all P < 0.05). Treatment duration was significantly longer (9.68 vs. 2.98 days, P < 0.001), with 60.0% versus 13.3% receiving therapy for ≥7 days (P < 0.001), whereas daily dose did not differ (P = 0.900). In Firth penalized logistic regression, kidney disease (OR 8.72, 95% CI 3.11-26.31) and treatment duration ≥7 days (OR 10.83, 95% CI 4.08-31.61) were independently associated with coagulopathy, whereas age ≥65 years was not (OR 2.03, 95% CI 0.74-6.11; P = 0.171). At onset, PT, INR, and APTT were markedly prolonged but normalized after drug discontinuation (P < 0.001), whereas platelet counts remained stable (P > 0.05), a pattern consistent with vitamin K cycle inhibition. CONCLUSION: In univariate analysis, advanced age, renal impairment, heart failure, diabetes, diuretic/anticoagulant use, and treatment duration ≥7 days were identified as potential factors. Kidney disease and treatment duration ≥7 days remained independently associated in penalized logistic regression. These findings underscore the need for risk-stratified monitoring protocols and suggest prophylactic vitamin K may be considered in high-risk patients. Future prospective studies with biomarker profiling are warranted.

articles.title: From mitochondrial injury to organelle communication: a bibliometric analysis of mitochondria-associated membranes research in cardiovascular diseases.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Mitochondria-associated membranes (MAMs) are specialized contact sites between the endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria that regulate calcium homeostasis, energy metabolism, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dynamics, and cell fate. Increasing evidence indicates that MAM dysfunction contributes to the pathogenesis of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs). However, a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of this field is still lacking. This study aimed to systematically characterize the knowledge structure, research hotspots, and emerging trends of MAM research in CVDs. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Publications related to MAMs in CVDs were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC). Bibliometric analyses were performed using CiteSpace and VOSviewer. A PubMed sensitivity analysis was conducted to evaluate the robustness of the findings. RESULTS: A total of 864 publications were included. Annual publications increased steadily, with rapid growth after 2013. China produced the largest number of publications, whereas the United States showed the greatest academic influence and international collaboration. Keyword analyses identified mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, cell death, and heart failure as the major research themes. Timeline and burst analyses further revealed a shift from studies of mitochondrial injury and apoptosis to investigations of mitochondrial dynamics, metabolic regulation, and inter-organelle communication. In recent years, mitophagy, dynamics, inflammation, metabolism, and contact sites have emerged as the most active research frontiers. The PubMed sensitivity analysis showed broadly consistent publication trends, author profiles, and research themes, indicating that the main findings were generally stable across the two databases. CONCLUSION: This study systematically mapped the knowledge landscape and developmental trajectory of MAM research in CVDs. The field has evolved from focusing on oxidative stress and mitochondrial injury to emphasizing mitochondrial quality control, metabolic regulation, and organelle communication. Mitophagy, metabolic reprogramming, inflammatory signaling, and membrane contact site biology are likely to remain major research frontiers. These findings provide a comprehensive overview of the field and may facilitate future mechanistic studies and the development of MAM-targeted therapeutic strategies for cardiovascular diseases.

articles.title: Discovery of scutellarin as a MRGX2 agonist via MRGX2/CMC strategy and revelation of its pseudo-allergic mechanism.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Shu-Gan-Ning injection (SGN) is widely used clinically to treat hepatopathy, improve liver function, and enhance immunity. However, pseudo-allergic reactions (PARs) occur after administration and the causative compounds remain unclear. Therefore, it is of paramount importance to pinpoint the "culprit" compound in SGN and explore its underling mechanism. METHODS: Mas-related G protein-coupled receptor X2 cell membrane chromatography (MRGX2/CMC)-HPLC-MS was established and used to "capture" and identify risk components in SGN. The interactions between risk components and MRGX2 were investigated by integrating MRGX2/CMC detection, virtual docking, and frontal analysis assays. MRGX2-knockdown LAD2 cell models were used to verify the specific target of the risk components and the signaling pathways that trigger PARs. C57BL/6 mice were used to evaluate the PARs induced by hazardous compounds. The conditional knockout mice model was used to evaluate the key role of MAS-related G protein-coupled receptor, member B2 (MRGB2) in mast cells in vivo pseudo-allergic reaction induced by target compound. RESULTS: We identified scutellarin, baicalin, and oroxyloside as MRGX2-binding components in SGN. Affinity analysis revealed KD values of 2.69 × 10-7 M for scutellarin, 2.18 × 10-7 M for baicalin, and 7.21 × 10-7 M for oroxyloside. Functional assays showed that only scutellarin (5-100 μM) concentration-dependently induced mast cell degranulation, Ca2+ influx, and release of inflammatory mediators. MRGX2 knockdown (mRNA ∼50%, protein ∼70%) significantly attenuated these responses, and pathway analysis confirmed that scutellarin activates the PLCγ/PKC cascade via MRGX2. In vivo, scutellarin induced local paw swelling and Evans blue extravasation, as well as systemic hypothermia, with EC50 values of 0.92 mg/kg for temperature reduction and 1.82 mg/kg for Evans blue exudation. In mast cell-specific Mrgb2 conditional knockout (CKO) mice, scutellarin-induced paw swelling and Evans blue leakage were significantly reduced compared with wild-type mice, confirming the critical role of MRGB2 in mediating the pseudo-allergic response. DISCUSSION: Collectively, these findings identify scutellarin as an MRGX2 agonist and a pseudo-allergic risk compound in SGN, highlighting the need for quality control measures for scutellarin in baicalin-containing preparations.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes of angina treatment in coronary microvascular dysfunction: results of a multicenter observational study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD or CMVD), a major subtype of angina with non-obstructive coronary arteries, affects a substantial proportion of patients and represents an important unmet clinical need, particularly in China. Studies evaluating comparative treatment efficacy in angina populations, especially across CMVD and non-CMVD, remain limited. OBJECTIVE: To assess the efficacy of different therapeutic regimens (nicorandil vs. non-nicorandil treatment) among angina pectoris patients with CMVD. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of baseline and follow-up data from nine centres of the GREAT study, including patients with angina from nine hospitals in China treated with nicorandil or non-nicorandil regimens. Patients with and without CMVD (coronary angiography-derived index of microvascular resistance [caIMR], ≥25 vs. < 25) were included, and post-treatment differences in Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ) scores were compared between groups. RESULTS: A total of 1,259 patients with angina were included in this study. Among them, 429 patients had CMVD (caIMR ≥25), comprising 170 in the nicorandil group and 259 in the non-nicorandil group, while 830 patients did not have CMVD (nicorandil group, 319; non-nicorandil group, 511). After propensity score matching, the mean SAQ summary score (SAQ-SS) improvement in patients with CMVD, was greater in the nicorandil group than in the non-nicorandil group (mean change: 16.80 vs. 12.60, P = 0.044). Among patients without CMVD, nicorandil therapy resulted in significantly greater SAQ-SS improvement at respective timepoints (3 months: 15.68 vs. 12.15, P = 0.005; 6 months: 18.70 vs. 14.44, P < 0.001; 9 months: 18.11 vs. 15.07, P = 0.008). CONCLUSION: Nicorandil-based regimens may be associated with greater improvement in health status among angina patients with CMVD compared with non-nicorandil treatments.

articles.title: Adolescent social isolation and re-socialization increases alcohol intake and aversion-resistant drinking in male and female rats.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Adverse experiences during adolescence, especially social isolation, increases risk for alcohol use disorders (AUDs). Previous rodent studies of adolescent social isolation (ASI) encompassed all stages of adolescence and/or maintained isolation into adulthood, limiting identification of vulnerable stages of adolescence. Utilizing males only, or combining the sexes, also may have contributed to contradictory findings. OBJECTIVES: Investigate social isolation restricted to discrete adolescent stages in combination with re-socialization and then persistent alcohol drinking. Determine whether adolescent isolation during specific developmental time periods, with or without subsequent re-socialization, leads to increased alcohol drinking in males or females. METHODS: Male and female Wistar rats underwent one of six housing conditions: (1) isolation from postnatal day (P)21-42 followed by re-socialization (ASIR-Early), (2) isolation from P42-63 followed by re-socialization (ASIR-Late), or (3) continuous isolation from P21 onward (ASI), or (4​-6) one of three appropriate control treatments. Alcohol-related behaviors were assessed in adulthood using intermittent-access two-bottle choice drinking (IAP), limited daily access (LDA-20) procedures, quinine-adulterated aversion-resistant drinking (ARD), and alcohol re-exposure following prolonged abstinence. RESULTS: In general, ASIR-Early and ASI elevated alcohol drinking in males and females, when compared to contemporary controls, during IAP, LDA-20, ARD, and after prolonged withdrawal, while ASIR-Late had largely similar effects as control conditions. However, for females, only ASI led to greater ARD at the highest quinine dose and also increased alcohol drinking after prolonged withdrawal. In contrast, for males, ASIR-Early and ASI had largely similar enhancement of alcohol drinking. CONCLUSIONS: Under these conditions, isolation housing that encompassed the early adolescent period produced enduring increases in alcohol-related behaviors, with re-socialization perhaps more protective in females against ARD and elevated intake after abstinence. These results inform future studies that will investigate neural mechanisms underlying ASI-induced enhancement of alcohol drinking.

articles.title: Biochanin A attenuates dexamethasone-induced skeletal muscle atrophy with increased SERCA2 expression and reduced mitochondrial injury.
articles.abstract: Glucocorticoid-induced skeletal muscle atrophy involves disrupted proteostasis, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and Ca2⁺ homeostasis. SERCA2 may connect Ca2⁺ handling with atrophy signaling. This study aimed to identify and evaluate a candidate intervention for dexamethasone (DEX)-induced skeletal muscle atrophy using SERCA2 expression as a mechanistic lead. Public transcriptomic analysis, in silico gene perturbation, and computational drug screening were integrated to identify potential anti-muscle atrophy compounds. The protective effects of Biochanin A (BCA) were subsequently evaluated in dexamethasone (DEX)-induced C2C12 myotube and mouse muscle atrophy models. ATP2A2 overexpression and siRNA knockdown, combined with molecular, morphological, and mitochondrial functional assays, were performed to investigate the anti-atrophic mechanism of BCA and its association with SERCA2. Computational screening identified Biochanin A (BCA) as a candidate anti-atrophy agent. In vitro, BCA attenuated DEX-induced atrophy marker expression and alleviated mitochondrial damage in C2C12 myotubes without significantly affecting apoptosis. ATP2A2 overexpression increased SERCA2 levels and reduced DEX-associated atrophy-related proteins, whereas BCA-associated reductions in selected proteins were less apparent in the independently normalized siATP2A2 series. In vivo, BCA attenuated DEX-induced losses in muscle mass and function while expanding myofiber size. Consistent with cellular results, BCA upregulated SERCA2 and downregulated p-SMAD3 and S100A4 protein levels in skeletal muscle tissues, whereas total SMAD3 protein expression did not differ significantly. BCA attenuated DEX-induced skeletal muscle atrophy in the experimental models. ATP2A2 overexpression and knockdown altered several atrophy-related protein responses, and BCA coadministration was accompanied by higher SERCA2 expression and reduced mitochondrial injury.

articles.title: Lenabasum attenuates CLP-induced sepsis-associated acute lung injury with coordinated modulation of redox balance and inflammation-resolution profile.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated acute lung injury is a major experimental counterpart of human acute respiratory distress syndrome and involves inflammatory activation, redox imbalance, and structural lung damage. Lenabasum (JBT-101), a selective cannabinoid receptor type 2 (CB2) agonist, has shown anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory properties in non-septic inflammation, but its effects in acute polymicrobial sepsis-associated lung injury remain poorly defined. This study evaluated lenabasum in a cecal ligation and puncture (CLP)-induced polymicrobial sepsis model during the acute 24-h phase, focusing on lung oxidative/antioxidant indices, the serum inflammation-resolution profile, and histopathological changes. 30 male Wistar rats were allocated to Sham, CLP, CLP + lenabasum 1 mg/kg, CLP + lenabasum 5 mg/kg, or CLP + dexamethasone 1 mg/kg groups. Interventions were administered intraperitoneally after sepsis induction. At 24 h, lung reactive oxygen species (ROS), malondialdehyde (MDA), and reduced glutathione (GSH) were measured. Serum tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), interleukin-8 (IL-8), C-reactive protein (CRP), and lipoxin A4 (LXA4) were assessed as the inflammation-resolution profile. Lung injury was evaluated under blinded conditions using hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) staining and lung injury score (LIS). CLP increased lung ROS and MDA, decreased GSH, elevated serum TNF-α, IL-8, CRP, and LXA4, and induced histopathological lung injury. Both lenabasum doses reduced MDA, serum inflammatory markers, and LIS and shifted LXA4 toward Sham levels. At 5 mg/kg, lenabasum also reduced ROS, increased GSH, and attenuated histopathological lung injury. Lenabasum, particularly at 5 mg/kg, attenuated biochemical disturbances and histopathological lung injury at 24 h after CLP. These findings support further preclinical investigation of lenabasum, while the receptor dependence of its effects remains to be established.

articles.title: Integration of machine learning and transcriptomics analysis identifies candidate molecular associations between parthenolide and sepsis-associated acute lung injury.
articles.abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) are both life-threatening diseases. Sepsis-related ALI frequently presents with complications of sepsis, which are mostly identified by the presence of non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema and refractory hypoxia. Despite the advancements in the field of drug discovery and delivery science, the understanding and management of sepsis-associated ALI are insufficient. WGCNA and differential expression analyses were integrated across multiple transcriptomics database cohorts to determine the core common candidate genes associated with sepsis-associated ALI and PTL. A Lasso model with SHAP interpretability was trained for feature selection. Molecular docking was performed for all candidate targets using PyRx with AutoDock Vina as the docking engine. Intersection of predicted parthenolide (PTL) targets and ALI-associated genes yielded 17 candidate genes. The Lasso algorithm used nested cross-validation, yielding an AUC of 0.827 (95% CI 0.767-0.928) and external validation with AUC values of 0.918 (GSE76293) and 0.667 (GSE10361). Molecular docking analysis indicated that the potential binding energies of the selected targets were - 5.9 to - 8.5 kcal/mol. These computational findings identify candidate PTL-associated molecular targets and provide a structural hypothesis to guide experimental validation.

articles.title: Bioactive laponite-reinforced thermosensitive PVA/Pluronic F127 hydrogel incorporating PRP and β-glucan: formulation, characterization, and preliminary in vivo evaluation.
articles.abstract: Beta-glucans are natural polysaccharides with immunomodulatory, anti-inflammatory, and tissue-regenerative properties, while platelet-rich plasma (PRP) supplies growth factors supporting cell proliferation and angiogenesis. We formulated and characterized a thermosensitive, sprayable hydrogel combining polyvinyl alcohol (PVA), Pluronic F127, Laponite, beta-glucan, and PRP, designed to be semi-liquid at room temperature and to gel near body temperature (37 °C) for in situ application to irregular wounds. A three-factor Box-Behnken design was used to investigate formulation composition and gelation-related properties. A practical formulation containing 3.5% (w/v) PVA, 10% (w/v) Poloxamer 407, 4% (w/v) Laponite, 2% (w/v) β-glucan, and 1% (v/v) PRP was selected for experimental characterization based on gelation temperature, gelation time, and stability. Rheological analysis demonstrated temperature-dependent viscoelastic behavior, while FTIR and SEM provided information on possible intermolecular interactions and the morphology of the freeze dried hydrogel. Mass-loss testing revealed limited persistence under the investigated aqueous conditions. The formulation was evaluated in a full-thickness excisional wound model in Wistar rats over a 14-day observation period. Wound area and diameter did not differ significantly among groups (P = 0.274 and P = 0.582, respectively). Blinded semi-quantitative histology (n = 3 per group per time point) showed normal healing progression in all groups with only small differences among groups (not statistically tested); the complete beta-glucan/PRP formulation showed numerical trends toward higher scores at day 14. These findings support the feasibility of the developed hydrogel as a thermoresponsive topical formulation; however, enhanced wound healing efficacy was not demonstrated, and further formulation refinement and biological evaluation are required.

articles.title: Inflammation at the Crossroads of UV Radiation and Pollution: The Molecular Synergy Behind Accelerated Skin Aging.
articles.abstract: The skin exposome which is the cumulative sum of environmental exposures and their biological imprint from conception to death remains an underexplored driver of premature skin aging, despite the skin's unique accessibility as a model organ. Ultraviolet (UV) radiation and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), notably benzo[a]pyrene (BaP), are two of the most pervasive and co-occurring extrinsic stressors acting directly on the skin surface. While each independently disrupts redox homeostasis, genomic integrity, and immune function, their combined exposure produces a supra-additive, non-linear interaction now termed "oxinflammation" whose magnitude depends critically on UV dose, pollutant concentration, and exposure duration, ranging from adaptive responses at low, acute exposures to persistent, maladaptive inflammatory activation under chronic, cumulative co-exposure. Building on this dose- and time-dependent framework, and extending beyond prior reviews that have treated UV and air pollution as parallel or additive threats to skin aging, this review centers on the immuno-inflammatory circuitry underlying their synergy particularly crosstalk between the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR), mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), and NF-κB pathways and its role in driving chronic low-grade inflammation ("inflammaging"), cellular senescence, and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) accumulation. We further examine PAH-driven immunomodulation and skin microbiome disruption as emerging, underappreciated contributors to this inflammatory circuit. Recent proteomic, metabolomic, and epigenetic evidence is synthesized to describe how this interplay impairs autophagy and DNA repair, degrades collagen through matrix metalloproteinase and cathepsin activation, and compromises epidermal barrier integrity, collectively accelerating extrinsic skin aging and contributing to the elevated carcinogenic risk associated with cumulative UV-pollutant co-exposure. We critically evaluate emerging therapeutic strategies including Nrf2 activators, mitochondria-targeted antioxidants, AhR antagonists, NAD+-restoring compounds, barrier-repair technologies, and microbiome-modulating interventions together with their translational limitations, such as poor cutaneous bioavailability of key candidate molecules. Finally, we outline future research priorities, emphasizing systematic dose-response characterization, multi-omics integration, advanced 3D and human-on-chip skin models, and personalized exposome analytics as necessary steps toward precision prevention of environmentally induced skin aging and its downstream oncological consequences.

articles.title: Future telling using nanovesicles: brain-derived, blood harvested extracellular vesicles for predicting human cognition fate.
articles.abstract: The human brain remains difficult to study due to its limited accessibility. The limited access constrains mechanistic insight into human cognition, one of the core functions of the central nervous system (CNS). Although advances in neuroimaging and molecular profiling have refined our understanding of the CNS complexity, the molecular correlates of cognitive functions in humans across the lifespan still remain obscure. In this context, blood-circulating extracellular vesicles (EVs) of the CNS origin have emerged as a promising approach to interrogate brain biology in vivo. CNS-derived EVs retain cell-type-enriched cargo and can cross the blood-brain barrier, making them attractive candidates for a "liquid biopsy" biomarkers of synaptic integrity, neuroglial interactions, and early neurodegenerative changes. Accumulating evidence indicates that peripheral EV cargo is related to cognitive status and may distinguish individuals at risk of cognitive impairment from those who remain resilient. This distinction may be potentially based on EV-encapsulated synaptic proteins, neuroinflammatory mediators, or disease-associated tau and amyloidβ species. Moreover, EV-based measures may provide a tractable framework for aligning preclinical and clinical data, linking neuroglial mechanisms and task performance in animal models with cognitive trajectories in human longitudinal cohorts. This perspective mini-review evaluates the potential of the CNS-derived EVs circulating in peripheral blood as biomarkers of life-long cognitive states across neurodevelopment, adulthood, and aging. I discuss evidence that EV cargo profiles change across the lifespan and may capture dynamic shifts in synaptic function and network vulnerability. The article outlines key barriers to clinical translation, including challenges in standardizing EV isolation and characterization in line with MISEV guidelines, issues of reproducibility and cell-type attribution, and the need for integrated multi-omic and multimodal approaches to improve the specificity and predictive value of EV-based cognitive biomarkers.

articles.title: Lorlatinib-associated sensorineural deafness in a non-small cell lung cancer patient with ALK-fusion: a Case Report.
articles.abstract: In the era of precision targeted therapy, anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) have significantly improved survival outcomes for patients with ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The third-generation ALK inhibitor lorlatinib, characterized by superior antitumor activity, a broader spectrum of ALK mutation sites and enhanced central nervous system (CNS) penetrability, has yielded breakthrough clinical benefits. However, lorlatinib has a distinct adverse event profile, with edema, dyslipidemia, central and peripheral nervous system toxicities, posing key clinical management challenges. Herein, we report the first case of an ALK-fusion NSCLC patient who developed peripheral neuropathy, dysarthria, and sensorineural deafness following lorlatinib treatment. While dysarthria and peripheral neuropathy have been previously documented, sensorineural deafness is extremely rare, and no prior reports describe the concurrent and persistent onset of all three symptoms, underscoring the need for enhanced toxicity monitoring and patient education.

articles.title: Case Report: Raw grass carp gallbladder ingestion and acute liver injury.
articles.abstract: Raw grass carp gallbladder ingestion for folk medicinal purposes may cause severe acute liver injury driven by the hepatotoxin 5α-cyprinol sulfate, yet high-dose human poisoning cases remain infrequently documented. We report a 60-year-old male (60 kg body weight) who developed severe intoxication 22 h after consuming six raw gallbladders from grass carps of approximately 1.5 kg each. Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain and watery diarrhoea occurred within 2 hours of ingestion. Laboratory testing on admission demonstrated extreme hepatocellular injury (ALT 6285 U/L, AST 9321 U/L). Conventional hepatoprotective agents plus pre-hospital haemoperfusion yielded limited biochemical improvement. While admitted to the intensive care unit, the patient received one session of double plasma molecular adsorption system, three sessions of plasma exchange and four sessions of continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT, CVVHDF modality) alongside comprehensive supportive care. Liver function normalized within 14 hospital days; no acute kidney injury was observed. Complete symptomatic recovery was documented at the 4-week follow-up visit, though longer-term outcomes remain unknown given the limited follow-up duration. Toxin-mediated hepatocyte damage is partially supported by pre-clinical cyprinol-sulfate experimental work; many downstream oxidative, mitochondrial, endoplasmic-reticulum and inflammatory molecular pathways remain hypothetical and are largely extrapolated from unrelated liver-injury models, without direct validation in human carp-gallbladder-poisoning tissue specimens. Biochemical improvement was temporally associated with multimodal extracorporeal purification, but causal therapeutic benefit can't be proven from this uncontrolled single case; spontaneous hepatic regeneration may also contribute to recovery. This case highlights substantial hazards associated with folk-health beliefs promoting raw fish-gallbladder consumption, emphasising the need for early clinical recognition of fish-gallbladder poisoning.

Selected carboxyl-group bioisosteres of mycophenolic acid with divergent biological profiles.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mycophenolic acid (MPA) is an immunosuppressive inhibitor of inosine-5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase (IMPDH). Bioisosteric replacement of its carboxyl group may modulate potency, cellular selectivity, and the overall biological profile. This study compared cyclic 1,2,4-oxadiazole derivatives and non-cyclic carboxylate bioisosteres to assess their effects on histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6), IMPDH-related activity, redox properties, and cellular responses. METHODS: The compounds were synthesised by dehydrative cyclisation of MPA with amidoximes or by coupling reactions affording hydroxamic acid, hydrazide, and amide analogues. They were evaluated by molecular docking to IMPDH type 2 (IMPDH2) and HDAC6, HDAC6 enzymatic inhibition, metabolic cytotoxicity and flow-cytometric proliferation assays in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and T-Jurkat cells, guanosine monophosphate (GMP) rescue, and 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl radical scavenging. RESULTS: Docking showed scaffold-dependent binding patterns. Non-cyclic bioisosteres showed more MPA-like predicted IMPDH2 binding modes and, when bearing zinc-binding groups, were more compatible with the zinc-containing HDAC6 catalytic region, whereas oxadiazoles adopted alternative predicted binding modes. In the HDAC6 enzymatic assay, pyridyl oxadiazoles were the most active cyclic derivatives, while the hydroxamic acid derivative showed nanomolar inhibition. In T-Jurkat cells, the newly synthesised derivatives showed substantially lower cytotoxic potency than MPA and mycophenolate mofetil (MMF), while several retained measurable antiproliferative activity. GMP rescue suggested functional divergence: non-cyclic bioisosteres showed GMP-rescuable antiproliferative effects consistent with guanine nucleotide depletion, whereas selected oxadiazoles were not rescued under these conditions. The antioxidant assay highlighted hydroxamic and hydrazide derivatives and the 2-furanyl oxadiazole. CONCLUSIONS: Carboxyl-group bioisosterism of MPA reshaped enzyme inhibition, redox activity, and cellular profiles. Non-cyclic derivatives retained GMP-rescuable antiproliferative profiles, with the hydroxamic acid analogue exhibiting particularly strong HDAC6 inhibition, whereas 1,2,4-oxadiazoles generally showed reduced cytotoxic potency and distinct cellular response patterns.

articles.title: Integrating AI-Guided Design with Experimental Validation for Niosome-Based Drug Delivery Systems.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop and experimentally validate an explainable artificial intelligence (AI) framework that extracts formulation rules for niosomal drug delivery systems from published data and delivers them through a decision-support platform. SIGNIFICANCE: Niosome performance depends on many interacting formulation and process variables, and optimization still relies largely on trial-and-error experimentation. Converting existing formulation knowledge into interpretable, experimentally verified rules could make early-stage development faster and less resource-intensive. METHODS: A database of 33 optimized niosomal formulations (approximately 30 drugs, BCS classes I-V) was compiled from peer-reviewed studies. Correlation analysis, XGBoost feature importance, and SHAP were used to relate formulation variables to particle size, entrapment efficiency (EE%), drug release, and release time. The extracted trends were tested experimentally using 17 diclofenac sodium-loaded niosomal formulations prepared by thin-film hydration. The dataset was expanded to 1000 samples using SMOTE to train XGBoost predictive models, which were evaluated on the original formulations and integrated with a Qwen-based large language model. RESULTS: Phosphate-buffered saline as the hydration medium, Span 60, and chloroform volume were the most influential variables. Laboratory results agreed with the AI-predicted direction of effect for all tested variables: cholesterol, Span 60, chloroform volume, Tween 80, and hydration medium. The predictive models achieved R2 values of 0.97-0.99 on the original formulations, and the resulting Niosome AI Expert platform showed general agreement between predicted and reported outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: Combining machine learning, explainable AI, and experimental verification can convert existing formulation knowledge into a practical decision-support tool that reduces reliance on trial-and-error niosome development.
